POSITION OVERVIEW
As a Senior Business Advisor, Strategy within BDC Advisory Services, you act as a senior strategic advisor to entrepreneurs and executive teams at pivotal moments of growth, transformation, and ownership transition. BDC is the only bank dedicated exclusively to Canadian entrepreneurs, and your work directly supports the long‑term success of small and medium‑sized businesses across Canada.
This position resides in Advisory Services (management consulting) and will serve Canadian Small and Medium Entrepreneurs through our consulting mandates. This is not a Financing role. The ideal candidate will have strong business strategy consulting experience with M&A (mergers and acquisitions) and PMI (post-merger integration) experience. The ideal candidate will have a vision for the future of business in an AI driven world and will have supported the consulting sales cycle and management of a portfolio of projects delivered by consultants.
CHALLENGES TO BE MET
Lead complex, high‑impact advisory mandates for entrepreneurs and senior leadership teams, focused on enterprise‑level strategic planning, growth acceleration, organizational effectiveness, and leadership decision‑making within SME and mid‑market environments.
Maintain full accountability for mandate outcomes across multiple concurrent engagements, ensuring delivery excellence related to scope, budget, timelines, risk management, and quality of deliverables.
Act as a trusted senior advisor during periods of ambiguity, transformation, and change, applying market insight, competitive analysis, and practical experience to guide high‑stakes decisions.
Contribute to the evolution of the Strategy Centre of Expertise by developing, refining, and scaling advisory solutions, tools, and methodologies aligned with emerging client needs and market trends.
Support business development and revenue growth by partnering with senior client managers on complex sales cycles, including executive‑level diagnostics, value articulation, and proposal development.
Enable strong internal collaboration by connecting advisors, delivery teams, and relationship managers, ensuring continuity of client strategy and effective knowledge transfer across engagements.
Represent BDC Advisory Services externally through thought leadership, content development, speaking engagements, and participation in targeted events that promote Business and Organizational Capabilities solutions. At BDC, we think and act differently, and we value inclusion, equity, and authenticity—you can be yourself at work while making a tangible impact on Canadian businesses.
WHAT WE ARE LOOKING FOR
Required Qualifications (Must‑Have)
Bachelor’s degree in Business, Management, Strategy, or a related discipline.
Minimum
10 years of progressive experience
in a consulting environment, with senior responsibility for:
Enterprise‑level strategic planning
Executive advisory to entrepreneurs and senior management teams
Leading complex, customized consulting mandates
Demonstrated experience advising SMEs or mid‑market organizations.
Proven experience in
business strategy consulting
, including
mergers and acquisitions (M&A)
and
post‑merger integration (PMI)
.
Ability to operate at both strategic and execution levels, translating enterprise strategy into actionable, measurable plans.
Strong engagement and project management capabilities, including oversight of
multiple concurrent mandates or portfolios of work
.
Experience managing risk, quality, governance, and stakeholder expectations across consulting engagements.
Executive‑level communication and presentation skills, with credibility to influence senior stakeholders and support high‑stakes advisory and sales conversations.
Experience supporting consulting business development activities, including diagnostics, proposal development, and client pursuits.
Preferred Qualifications (Nice‑to‑Have)
MBA or equivalent advanced degree or professional designation.
Experience contributing to the development or scaling of consulting methodologies, tools, or Centres of Expertise.
Exposure to
emerging technologies
, including
artificial intelligence
, and their impact on enterprise strategy and organizational transformation.
Experience managing or overseeing a
portfolio of consulting projects delivered by other consultants
.
Experience representing a consulting practice through thought leadership, speaking engagements, or external market visibility initiatives.

Join a team shaping Canada’s venture capital ecosystem
At BDC, the Government Funds team manages capital on behalf of the Government of Canada to strengthen and grow Canada’s venture capital market. This includes deploying
$350M under the Venture Capital Action Plan (VCAP)
,
$450M under the Venture Capital Catalyst Initiative (VCCI)
, and
$450M under the Renewed Venture Capital Catalyst Initiative (Renewed VCCI)
. These programs totalling $1.2B AUM are designed to
crowd in private capital
and support fund managers across the Canadian venture capital asset class.
Building on this foundation, BDC is now deploying the
$1B Growth Venture Capital Catalyst Initiative (Growth VCCI)
, a landmark platform focused on scaling Canada’s most promising funds and innovative companies.
This is a unique opportunity to work at the intersection of
investment, policy, and ecosystem development
, with direct exposure to the most prominent Canadian fund managers while contributing to a
national priority initiative shaping Canada’s innovation economy
.
POSITION OVERVIEW
As Director, you will combine leadership, investment expertise, and complex project management to support the deployment and oversight of government-backed venture capital programs, including VCAP, VCCI, Renewed VCCI, and upcoming Growth VCCI.
You will play a lead role in investment execution, stakeholder management, and portfolio governance, while engaging closely with fund managers, institutional partners, and internal stakeholders including Government.
CHALLENGES TO BE MET
Investment Expertise
Lead complex business and legal negotiations with fund managers and external stakeholders for execution of program delivery including fund investments.
Provide strategic oversight of investment activities across the portfolio, ensuring alignment between policy objectives, portfolio construction considerations, and market dynamics
Provide senior investment judgment and guidance on fund performance, risk management, and portfolio development matters
Fund Oversight & Governance
Serve as BDC’s representative on portfolio funds’ LPACs and other governance bodies
Monitor fund performance, governance, and compliance with fund agreements and program requirements
Provide strategic insight and constructive challenge to support strong governance practices and enhance fund outcomes
Guide fund managers on governance and operational best practices to strengthen the long-term sustainability of the venture capital ecosystem
Leadership and Team Management
Demonstrate leadership in team meetings and operations processes, ensuring effective resource allocation, quality control, operational excellence, and alignment with strategic priorities
Ensure the timely and accurate execution of operational activities, including capital calls, distributions, reporting, and stakeholder deliverables
Provide coaching, mentorship, and leadership to a team of Analysts, fostering a collaborative, high-performance culture focused on continuous improvement and professional development
Identify capability and capacity gaps, oversee recruitment and onboarding activities, and promote knowledge sharing and best practices across the team
Program Delivery & Stakeholder Management
Provide strategic input into the design, implementation, and continuous improvement of current and future government investment programs
Respond to complex and time-sensitive requests from internal and external stakeholders while maintaining a high standard of service and professionalism
Oversee the preparation and dissemination of quarterly and annual reporting, performance dashboards, and stakeholder communications
Ensure high standards of quality, consistency, accuracy, and timeliness across all reporting outputs and program deliverables
Portfolio & Ecosystem Leadership
Build and maintain strong relationships with fund managers, institutional investors, ecosystem stakeholders, and government partners
Represent BDC Capital and Government Funds at industry conferences, panels, events, and stakeholder forums
Stay closely connected to venture capital trends, market developments, and emerging opportunities to support strategic decision-making
Support and lead thought leadership initiatives, market studies, and research projects that generate insights from government investment programs and portfolio activities
WHAT WE ARE LOOKING FOR
Experience and qualifications
Minimum of a Bachelor degree in Commerce or a related discipline (finance, accounting, law or business administration preferred), or an equivalent combination of academic training and relevant professional experience
10 years+ experience in venture capital, private equity, or growth investing, with direct exposure to deal-making at the fund level as well as investment underwriting, structuring, business and legal negotiations and execution
Demonstrated expertise in venture capital fund structures, LPAs, governance frameworks, and policy-driven investment programs
Demonstrated ability to lead complex negotiations and manage multiple high-priority initiatives simultaneously
Significant experience serving on LPACs, Boards of Directors, or equivalent governance bodies
Ability to manage complex stakeholder relationships involving fund managers, institutional investors, government representatives, and senior executives
Strong understanding of the Canadian venture capital ecosystem and a well-established network of industry relationships
Experience leading, coaching, and developing high-performing teams
Core competencies
Strong strategic and investment judgment
Demonstrated leadership and people management capabilities
Excellent communication, influencing, and stakeholder management skills
Ability to align operational execution with broader policy, program, and organizational objectives
High level of rigour, organization, and attention to detail
Ability to operate effectively in a complex, fast-paced, multi-stakeholder environment
Collaborative mindset with a commitment to team development, knowledge sharing, and excellence
The position is primarily based in Montreal or Ottawa, with a preference for these locations. Toronto is also acceptable.

The Growth Venture Fund team operates within BDC Capital and is focused on growing and scaling the next generation of Canadian venture-backed champions. Currently investing out of the 500M$ Growth Venture Fund, our participations range from $5M to 40M in late stage (>$10M in revenues) innovation-based businesses in Canada that are at an inflection point and show strong potential for meaningful scale, across a broad range of technology sectors. The Growth Venture Fund team currently manages 28 active late-stage companies.
POSITION OVERVIEW
Reporting to the managing partner of the Growth Venture Fund and working collaboratively with partners, principals, associates and analysts, the Associate is an integral member of the BDC Capital team and is involved in all aspects of the investment and portfolio management process.
They will participate in the review of investment opportunities and assist in managing an existing legacy portfolio and new investments for all of the funds we manage.
CHALLENGES TO BE MET
Contribute to due diligence for new and/or existing investment opportunities by conducting research and analysis on markets, financial forecasts, management, competition, etc. and follow-up on investments using appropriate databases, customer interaction, internet sites, research reports and other investment resources
Assist in account updates by providing financial, forecasting and statistical analysis and bringing potential issues to partners’ attention
Ensure that new and existing investments files are properly documented (on initial investments, reinvestments and exits), including financial analysis and forecasting
Ensure the accuracy and timeliness of data by developing and maintaining appropriate information resources and contacts on industries, markets and business trends and keeping abreast of significant developments and activities in the venture capital and innovation communities
Ensure that the investment research files, business plans and other information collected by the Growth Venture Fund are maintained in conformity with BDC’s policies and procedures
Monitor the investment portfolio and individual companies by providing financial, forecast and statistical analysis to ensure timely responsiveness to strategic issues within the funds
Support other Growth Venture Fund team members across the full lifecycle of an investment
WHAT WE ARE LOOKING FOR
Intellectual curiosity, solid analytical and synthesis skills, ability to assess the merits of new technologies, size and adoption rates of new markets and competitive forces faces when introducing new products
Possesses high energy towards work and self-development
Ability to work under pressure, deal with abstract concepts, an unstructured environment and multi-tasking
Ability to prepare financial forecasts, advanced financial models and pro-forma financial statements
Strong communication capabilities, including the ability to produce and deliver clear and concise oral and written presentations in English

Bachelor’s degree in either Business Administration, Commerce, Science or Engineering.

You will be responsible for proposing high quality loan proposals in the amount of $1M or more, for businesses in various industries across Canada. POSITION OVERVIEW
The Senior Manager, Underwriting is responsible for conducting proper investigations and due diligence activities for loan proposals. The Manager, Underwriting, must also present high-quality proposals, which include all appropriate analysis and documentation while ensuring that risk levels are within the parameters of accepted credit practices and BDC policies and procedures.
CHALLENGES TO BE MET
Underwrite high-quality proposals by analyzing and conducting proper investigations and due diligence for medium to high complexity loan proposals.
Develop appropriate terms, pricing, conditions and covenants while ensuring thorough credit analysis, due diligence and sound account management practices.
Review loan packages and, when necessary, negotiate with internal partners (AM/BCM/CRM) on structuring the deal to ensure compliance with BDC policies and procedures.
Participate in the resolution of compliance or material changes that arise as deals are being negotiated and structured.
Develop win-win solutions for the client and BDC through innovative thinking and resourcefulness.
Maintain relationships with business centre personnel, colleagues and internal partners in order to foster teamwork, the pursuit of common objectives and the consistent application of policies.
Keep abreast of changes to policies, procedures and detailed processes and trends in credit and regulatory issues that may have an impact on BDC.
Coach new employees and BDLs; mentor and share experience with team members.
WHAT WE ARE LOOKING FOR
Bachelor’s degree in commerce, business administration or accounting
Accounting designation or CFA and banking experience are a definite asset
3 to 5  years or more of relevant experience
Experience in corporate and/or syndicated financing
Experience in loan writing and ability to analyze and structure complex financial deals
Sound credit judgement coupled with a strong understanding of credit policies and practices
Thorough knowledge of Bank products, services, policies and procedures and ability to provide high quality customer service to internal/external clients

This role offers an opportunity to apply strong analytical skills, seasoned credit judgment, and commercial lending experience in support of Canadian entrepreneurs. You will prepare and authorize well-supported loan proposals for businesses across a range of industries and regions, contributing to prudent credit decision-making and responsible portfolio growth. If you are looking to join an organization that invests in your development, values diverse perspectives, and supports meaningful work, we invite you to be part of our committed team.
POSITION OVERVIEW
At BDC, the only bank dedicated exclusively to Canadian entrepreneurs, your work will help advance the growth and long-term success of small and medium-sized businesses across the country.
As Senior Manager, Underwriting – Credit Risk Management, you will be accountable for credit due diligence, risk analysis, and the authorization of loan proposals of moderate to high complexity. You will develop well-supported proposals that reflect BDC’s credit risk standards and align with established policies and procedures. At BDC, you can be yourself at work in an inclusive environment where expertise, collaboration, and meaningful impact are recognized and valued.
CHALLENGES TO BE MET
Underwrite and authorize comprehensive, well-structured loan proposals for moderate to high complexity credit files, ranging from $350,000 to $1.5 million, through detailed financial analysis, appropriate investigation, and thorough due diligence.
Determine appropriate credit terms, pricing, repayment structures, and covenants while applying disciplined credit analysis, balanced risk assessment, and effective account management practices.
Review loan documentation and, when required, negotiate transaction structures with internal partners, including account managers and business centre management, to ensure alignment with BDC policies and procedures.
Support the resolution of compliance matters and material changes that arise during transaction negotiation and structuring, ensuring appropriate risk mitigation and timely decision-making.
Develop practical, well-suited solutions that meet the needs of both the client and BDC by applying sound judgment, creativity, and strong problem-solving skills.
Build and maintain trusted working relationships with business centre colleagues and internal partners to foster collaboration, support shared objectives, and promote consistent application of credit policies.
Stay current on changes to credit policies, procedures, and processes, as well as emerging credit and regulatory trends that may affect BDC.
Provide coaching to new employees, act as a mentor, and actively support knowledge sharing within the team and with internal partners.
WHAT WE ARE LOOKING FOR
Bachelor’s degree in commerce, business administration, accounting, or a related field.
CPA or CFA designation considered a strong asset.
Bilingualism in English and French considered a strong asset.
Minimum of five (5) years of relevant experience in credit analysis, loan adjudication, commercial lending, or a related financial services role.
Experience coaching, mentoring, or guiding colleagues in a team environment.
Demonstrated ability to analyze, structure, and assess commercial financing transactions.
Strong credit judgment and a solid understanding of credit risk policies, practices, and governance expectations.
Knowledge of BDC products, services, policies, processes, and procedures, or the ability to quickly develop this knowledge.
Excellent communication skills, with the ability to interact, influence, and negotiate effectively with internal partners and, when required, with clients.
Strong organizational skills and the ability to manage competing priorities while meeting critical deadlines in a high-volume environment.
Solid business acumen and a strong understanding of the realities and dynamics of small and medium-sized enterprises.

POSITION OVERVIEW
BDC Capital’s Industrial Innovation Venture Fund backs ambitious founders rebuilding the industrial economy. We invest in companies using software, hardware, AI, robotics, advanced materials, climate technologies, and deep tech to transform sectors such as manufacturing, agriculture, energy, infrastructure, and resources.
We are looking for an Investment Associate who wants to be close to the edge of industrial disruption: meeting exceptional founders, pressure-testing breakthrough technologies, mapping emerging markets, and helping Canadian companies scale into global category leaders. This is a highly analytical, founder-facing role for someone with curiosity, rigour, speed, and strong commercial judgment.
CHALLENGES TO BE MET
Source and Shape the Pipeline
Build conviction on emerging industrial technology markets and identify companies before they are obvious
Develop relationships with founders, investors, operators, researchers, and strategic partners across the ecosystem
Maintain sharp market maps, sector theses, founder lists, and deal-tracking tools that help the fund move with speed and discipline
Evaluate Breakthrough Companies
Assess startups across market size, product differentiation, customer value, go-to-market, team quality, business model, cap table, and exit potential
Run diligence workstreams including customer calls, expert interviews, founder sessions, technical reviews, financial modeling, and investment memo preparation
Turn complex technical and commercial inputs into clear, decision-ready investment recommendations
Support Portfolio Companies
WHAT WE ARE LOOKING FOR
Your Background
4+ years of experience in venture capital, private equity, investment banking, consulting, corporate strategy, corporate development, a technology startup, or an industrial/technical operating role
Strong analytical foundation, ideally supported by a degree in commerce, economics, science, technology, engineering, mathematics, or a related field
Comfort with financial modeling, market research, customer discovery, technical diligence, and synthesizing ambiguity into clear recommendations
Your Edge
You are intellectually curious and excited by hard industrial problems, technical founders, and markets where adoption is difficult but impact is massive
You can engage confidently with founders, executives, investors, operators, customers, and technical experts
You communicate crisply, write clearly, and can make complex technologies understandable to investment and executive audiences
You are proactive, resourceful, low-ego, and energized by fast-moving, high-ambiguity environments
Technical skills, operating experience in an industrial sector, and bilingualism in French and English are assets
Why Join Us
You will work with a focused venture team backing founders at the frontier of industrial transformation. The role offers exposure to category-defining companies, complex technologies, active investment decisions, and a national platform committed to helping Canadian entrepreneurs build globally relevant businesses.

Job Summary
CBC Sports is looking for an Executive Producer for the 2028 Summer Olympic Games. Reporting to the Executive Director, the successful candidate will be a key member of the leadership team of CBC Olympics.  This position will work closely with two other Executive producers who oversee different aspects of the production.
We are looking for an experienced producer who will push the boundaries of traditional broadcasting. As an editorial leader for the LA28 Games, you will champion unconventional narratives, bold visual formats, and fresh ways to capture the human drama of the Olympics—actively seeking to expand our range and impact across all screens.
The Executive Producer is instrumental in assigning stories to be chased, monitoring development, creating a coverage plan for the Games, and contributing to the overall planning function of the Games. The successful candidate will also be expected to mentor, direct, and develop programming talent, producers, on-air talent, and hosts, as well as take an active role in department-wide and CBC initiatives.
Function
Plans, conceives, organizes, and/or develops the production and realization of a program segment, program, or series. Work must adhere to CBC journalistic and/or program policies, standards, and practices, and the Executive Producer is ultimately responsible for ensuring that this occurs. Nevertheless, there is wide latitude for initiative, independent judgment, and creativity. There is a regular and ongoing requirement to co-ordinate the work of others.
Key Tasks
Conceives, develops, and champions ground-breaking program concepts that challenge conventional sports production. You will use your creative latitude to design distinctive, non-traditional formats that seamlessly bridge live television and digital platforms, turning complex technical setups into canvas elements for immersive, high-impact storytelling.
Review the style, pace, tempo, and format of the broadcast. Rather than relying on standard sports templates, you will bring a fresh aesthetic and creative choreography to live multi-sport events, tailoring content dynamically for different audiences and platforms.
Develops the program content including assigning, researching, gathering, writing, and/or editing; as required, commissions writing/research and prepares scripts.

CBC News is looking for a creative editorial leader with sharp news judgement to lead our live and daily audio news programming on the weekends.
As Senior Producer, Live & Daily News, Weekend Late Audio you drive daily programming with a hyper-focus on live and breaking national and international news for our hourly radio news and podcast programs, Your World Tonight and The World This Hour.
You bring an audience-first mindset to the role, shaping compelling content that plays equally well as a podcast as it does on terrestrial radio. You are expected to steer daily editorial meetings, stimulate creative discussions, and identify the most impactful stories and treatments for the day.
You react decisively to major developments, track stories in real time and reshape shows on the fly to ensure our audiences are getting the content they need to know, now. You support your colleagues across the CBC News system when it pivots to extended live coverage. Extensive studio skills are essential to succeed in this fast-paced setting.
You care about the people you work with and have a deep appreciation for different perspectives, opinions and experiences. You live and promote the values of diversity and an inclusive and respectful work culture. You provide meaningful, constructive feedback; guide complex editorial decisions; and actively teach advanced writing and producing skills.
You ensure that all CBC journalistic standards are met and that our stories are fair, balanced, accurate, thoughtful, immediate and resonate with the communities we serve.
Reporting to the Executive Producer of Live & Daily News, Weekends, you help meet CBC’s strategic goals, including working across platforms to meet audience needs no matter where they consume our content.
Based in Toronto, this is a full-time, permanent position. The successful candidate will work a four-day compressed work week (Thursday to Sunday). Hours will be decided by operational requirements. You can expect some overtime, including early mornings and evenings when news is breaking.
Key Tasks
●
Editorial Direction:
Determine story priorities, develop innovative content strategies, and expertly guide teams through live, breaking, and ongoing news coverage. Guide the team on story length, deadlines, updates, and audio treatments.
●
Live Experience:
Develop & practise a culture of embracing breaking news and leaning into developing stories with a disciplined focus on audience needs and CBC News strategy. Collaborate with broadcast, streaming and digital to ensure a full live experience across all platforms.
●
Manage Production & Broadcast:
Exercise editorial responsibility over daily production and live broadcasting. Co-ordinate resources and determine the look, style, and pace of the lineup to maintain consistency with network mandates. Thrive under intense deadline pressures.
●
Change Agent:
Drives continuous improvement, agile and adaptable in transforming newsroom structures and roles and lead transitions. You understand what motivates people. You welcome feedback and carefully consider that input as you align your team around shared goals. You celebrate success.
●
Foster Collaboration:
Facilitate open, inclusive story meetings. Encourage story pitches and development. Collaborate across CBC News platforms to co-ordinate content, such raw sound, clipped material and packaged audio items.
●
Team Leadership:
Actively support staff development, provide ongoing constructive feedback and coaching. Connect regularly with senior leadership about staffing and scheduling requirements and team culture.
●
Champion Audience Growth:
Translate insights and data to guide content decisions to expand our reach to new and younger news consumers, and to deepen our engagement with all Canadians.
●
Maintain Standards:
Strictly uphold CBC’s Journalistic Standards and Practices at all times.
●
Operational Support:
Step in to perform all or part of the functions of an equivalent or lower classification as needed.

Experience:
Minimum of seven years in broadcast journalism, with a university degree or college diploma in journalism, audio production, or a related field.
●
Live Broadcast Expertise:
Proven experience producing live and breaking news programming, including production planning and resource co-ordination. Demonstrated ability as a programmer with a keen ear for pacing, tone, and presentation.
●
Technical Proficiency:
Mandatory experience taking programs to air, alongside highly developed audio production skills. Familiarity with technology including iNews, Dalet, Avid Media Central and Google tools for content creation, distribution, and planning.

Critical thinking:
Exceptional problem-solving skills to navigate fast-moving, high-pressure news situations. You're adept at verifying and fact-checking content.
●
Broad Knowledge Base:
Deep interest and understanding across topics such as politics, business, science, sports, entertainment, and health.
●
Mentorship Skills:
Superior coaching abilities to support developing journalists, veteran staff, and on-air hosts. Exceptional communication, organizational, and feedback skills.

A deep commitment to public broadcasting, understanding of modern industry trends, ability to identify legal and ethical issues in journalism, and application of CBC’s Journalistic Standards and Practices.

The Opportunity
Are you passionate about technology transformation, evolving operating models and shaping new ways of working from concept through to adoption? In this key role, you will serve as a strategic technology transformation adviser to leaders and teams, helping diagnose challenges, define and structure change initiatives, and drive operational implementation and adoption across the organization.
Reporting to the Director of the Operational Excellence Office within Technology & Infrastructure (T&I), you will join the team leading the Daily Content initiative in Innovation & Delivery. You will be joining us at a pivotal moment as CBC/Radio-Canada undergoes a major overhaul to modernize its content creation platforms. This transformation goes beyond software and tools — it redefines how production platforms are designed, delivered and used within an organizational model focused on product management, agile at scale, and continuous value creation.
In this role, you will combine a strategic consulting mindset with hands-on execution across all stages of the transformation. You will analyze complex issues, challenge established ways of working and provide actionable recommendations while actively driving their implementation by designing and producing the strategies, plans, frameworks, tools and other deliverables needed to execute and adopt the transformation.
Key areas of focus include transitioning to a product management model, modernizing collaboration with partners and contributors, and driving user adoption of new production tools. You will help define, structure and roll out the transformation and change management strategies required across all levels of the organization.
You will also play a central role in bringing together and aligning diverse teams and stakeholders across CBC/Radio-Canada around a shared vision and common goals. Your ability to grasp and navigate a complex organizational ecosystem, balance operational constraints and competing priorities, and exert influence without direct authority will be essential to align perspectives, build consensus, streamline decision-making and remove roadblocks.
Working alongside key stakeholders, you will support the organization in preparing for and implementing changes — including by developing and rolling out effective engagement and communications strategies — and by preparing and supporting end users in tandem with our Learning & Development partners.
You will work closely with operational and strategic leaders, as well as with the Daily Content Director, to structure challenges, shape recommendations and guide the evolution of work practices and production tools.
As a member of T&I’s Operational Excellence Office, you will help ensure alignment, practical execution and long-term adoption of the transformation by continuously refining our approaches based on results, key insights and frontline needs. Beyond the Daily Content initiative, you will also help build the Office’s methods, practices and capabilities as well as nurture a transformation community of practice across CBC/Radio-Canada to share lessons learned and scale high-impact practices.
This position can be based in Toronto or Montreal, with occasional travel required.
Key Responsibilities
Advise leaders and teams on defining and implementing technology transformations, engaging early in the life cycle to analyze needs, diagnose challenges, identify required changes and deliver recommendations aligned with the organization's vision and goals.
Guide departments and divisions in evolving their operating models and ways of working, advising on process design, governance, roles and responsibilities, and team collaboration structures.
Develop approaches, frameworks and tools to structure and implement transformation — including simple, scalable and reusable interaction models and practical guides — with a focus on change management, Lean, SAFe and Scrum methodologies.
Design and execute change management and adoption strategies and plans, incorporating impact assessments, organizational readiness, risk mitigation and stakeholder support.
Define and lead engagement, communication and capacity-building strategies — including user training and the preparation of delivery teams and change agents — in partnership with Learning & Development.
Proactively identify and resolve risks, resistance and operational roadblocks that could hinder transformation and adoption.
Define and track metrics to measure the progress, adoption and effectiveness of new ways of working, using data and insights to continuously refine strategies.
Actively participate in key transformation forums and events, including strategic and alignment meetings, sprint reviews, program demos and quarterly planning sessions.
What You Bring
Undergraduate degree in business administration, technology or a field relevant to organizational transformation (or an equivalent combination of education and relevant experience).
Seven to 10 years' experience leading large-scale technology transformations, including evolving technology operating models, processes, governance structures, roles and responsibilities, and ways of working within complex, matrixed environments.
Proven track record as a strategic transformation adviser, with strong skills in analyzing and diagnosing complex issues, challenging current practices, formulating actionable recommendations and guiding execution.
Solid understanding of product management models and agile practices at scale, with hands-on experience applying them to tech transformations. Expertise in SAFe (Scaled Agile Framework), Scrum or other scaled agile frameworks required.
Experience with Lean and iterative transformation approaches, alongside the ability to adapt strategies and solutions based on key insights, data and frontline needs.
Demonstrated experience in end-to-end change management and adoption, including impact analysis, stakeholder engagement, strategic communications and capability building.
Knowledge of media production, broadcasting workflows and related technologies (e.g., audio/video editing, publishing, distribution, graphics generation) a major asset.
Proven ability to navigate complex organizational dynamics (including labour relations), manage resistance, resolve conflict and build trust-based relationships with stakeholders at all levels.
Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, paired with sharp business acumen and the ability to synthesize complex challenges into clear, actionable recommendations and solutions.
Demonstrated ability to influence, guide and engage leaders and teams without direct authority.
Exceptional facilitation and active listening skills, with the ability to translate complex technical concepts into clear, plain language.
Bilingualism in English and French (written and spoken) required.

Our team combines industry expertise with commitment to public service. We attract individuals who are interested in

employer-matched
defined benefit pension plan
, and a comprehensive and competitive benefits plan. We prioritize learning and development, wellbeing, diversity, equity, inclusion and belonging, and community giving.
Join FSRA and help us shape the future of regulation for generations to come!
Job Description:
EXISTING VACANCY
Salary Range - $106,462 -$156,462 (salary will be determined based on the successful candidate's skills, experience and qualifications)
Purpose of Position
Accountable for managing the delivery of Market Conduct compliance of Mortgage Brokers including related programs and services in support of overall Market Conduct department strategies.
Key Responsibilities
Manages the delivery of programs and services aimed at regulating Mortgage Brokers regulated by FSRA; ensuring consistency with overall Market Conduct performance measures, standards, best practices and integration with overall FSRA directions.
As part of the management team, supports FSRA leadership in formulating strategy and developing tactics and provides leadership in executing programs or services to deliver on strategy and tactics.
Oversees the implementation of Mortgage Broker Market Conduct programs, services and work areas, including operational processes and procedures to meet the overall operational plans and priorities of the department.

Manages the provision of strategic expertise and support for the escalation of conduct matters including, where appropriate, enforcement referrals

Supports critical change and a new collaborative, forward thinking culture within the unit, and works with others to achieve this across the section or department.
Promotes and supports the implementation of innovation and continuous improvement throughout the unit and section or department.

Degree in law, accounting, commerce, business administration, engineering, mathematics, public policy, a related field or equivalent.
6 – 8 years’ experience in planning and managing the delivery of regulatory programs or services for    mortgage brokers regulated by FSRA combined with expertise in working as a member of a larger relevant regulatory department.

As a key member of the Risk Technology team, the Senior Data Engineer will be the team’s senior hands-on Power BI developer, responsible for designing complex reports and visuals, scalable semantic models, and governed business intelligence solutions. The successful candidate will be expected to apply a practical understanding of Fabric capacity, compute consumption, memory constraints, performance, and workload management.
The role also requires strong data engineering capability. The successful candidate will build and support reliable data pipelines that hydrate Power BI semantic models from enterprise data warehouses and will develop complex ETL and transformation solutions using Azure Databricks, Snowflake, Azure Data Factory, SQL, Python, and PySpark.
This position combines deep technical delivery with stakeholder partnership. The incumbent will collaborate with business users, business systems analysts, data engineers, platform teams, and external providers, and will contribute to a constructive, inclusive, and accountable team environment. The role follows the organization’s hybrid working model and requires regular in-office collaboration.
The incumbent will report to the Senior Manager, Data Technology.
As a Member of Our Team You Will be Responsible For:
Power BI development and reporting framework (Primary Area of Accountability)
Design, develop, test, deploy, and support sophisticated Power BI reports, dashboards, and interactive visual experiences for Investment Risk and related stakeholders.
Build and optimize enterprise-grade Power BI semantic models, including dimensional design, relationships, measures, calculation groups where appropriate, row-level security, object-level security, incremental refresh, and model performance tuning.
Write and optimize complex DAX and Power Query (M) logic, applying clear development standards and reusable design patterns.
Partner closely with business users to translate analytical requirements into intuitive visual designs, rapidly prototype solutions, validate usability, and incorporate feedback throughout delivery.
Understand and actively manage Fabric capacity considerations, including compute consumption, memory guardrails, concurrency, refresh demand, background versus interactive workloads, throttling risk, and workload optimization.
Use capacity and performance telemetry to identify bottlenecks, recommend remediation, and balance report responsiveness, refresh schedules, model size, and platform stability.
Design and support data pipelines that reliably hydrate Power BI semantic models from Snowflake, Databricks, enterprise data warehouses, lakehouses, and other approved data sources.
Implement governed Power BI access management, including workspaces, apps, audiences, Microsoft Entra security groups, role-based access, sharing, row-level security, deployment permissions, and periodic access reviews.
Design, build, test, and support Power Automate cloud flows that extend Power BI solutions through data-driven alerts, notifications, approvals, scheduled actions, and user-triggered workflows.
Apply appropriate Power Automate governance and support practices, including connection management, environment awareness, secure sharing, run monitoring, exception handling, and operational documentation.
Promote effective Power BI lifecycle management through source control, deployment pipelines, environment segregation, release controls, documentation, and CI/CD practices.
Data Engineering (Secondary Area of Accountability)
Develop complex, performant, and maintainable solutions in Azure Databricks and Snowflake using SQL, Python, and PySpark.
Develop and orchestrate data integration workflows using Azure Data Factory and other approved Azure data services.
Create and optimize database objects, data transformations, data quality controls, and reconciliation processes with a strong understanding of dimensional and analytical data modeling.
Build custom services and workflows when needed to complement platform capabilities, including file-format conversion, third-party API integration, and external web-service calls.
Automate manual processes and improve data delivery, observability, scalability, recoverability, and operational efficiency.
Contribute to solution architecture and technical design for the Databricks, Snowflake, Microsoft Fabric, and Azure data ecosystem.
Delivery, Operations and Collaboration
Work closely with business systems analysts, subject-matter experts, platform teams, and vendors to deliver solutions, investigate root causes, recommend changes, and maintain accurate technical and operational documentation.
Monitor production solutions, investigate incidents, perform performance tuning, and enhance service reliability through effective incident, problem, change, configuration, and release-management practices.
Prepare functional and technical specifications, data-flow documentation, support procedures, test evidence, deployment plans, and knowledge-transfer materials.
Facilitate testing and production implementation while acting as a trusted liaison between Technology, Investment Risk stakeholders, and external solution providers.
Share design, coding, troubleshooting, and analytical practices with colleagues through reviews, pairing, documentation, and knowledge sessions.
Demonstrate a constructive and collaborative working style, openness to feedback, accountability for outcomes, and willingness to support colleagues across disciplines.
Participate effectively in the organization’s hybrid working model, including regular in-office collaboration with the team and stakeholders.
What do you need to succeed?
Minimum 7 years of progressive experience in advanced Power BI development expertise, including complex report design, visual storytelling, semantic modeling, DAX, Power Query, model optimization, refresh design, and troubleshooting.
Experience of delivering data, analytics, data warehousing, or business intelligence solutions, with substantial recent hands-on Power BI development experience.
Demonstrated experience building governed, enterprise-scale Power BI solutions rather than solely creating ad hoc or departmental reports.
Hands-on Microsoft Fabric experience, or directly transferable experience with Power BI Premium capacity, including capacity monitoring, compute and memory constraints, workload management, performance tuning, and migration planning.
Experience designing and operating pipelines that load or transform data for Power BI semantic models from cloud data warehouses or Lakehouse platforms.
Practical experience administering Power BI access through workspaces, apps, audiences, security groups, permissions, and row-level security, with an understanding of least-privilege access and controlled content distribution.
Hands-on experience developing and supporting Power Automate cloud flows, ideally integrated with Power BI, Microsoft 365, approvals, alerts, or other enterprise services.
Minimum 3 years of Databricks experience with strong data engineering experience, including complex transformations and performance-aware development.
Advanced SQL skills, including complex queries, tables, views, stored procedures, query optimization, and performance tuning.
Proficiency in Python and PySpark for scalable data processing and automation.
Developed data warehouses with change data capture (CDC) and implemented dimensional data warehouses.
Understanding data quality, GitHub source control, CI/CD, and production support practices for enterprise BI and data solutions.
Strong communication, problem-solving, prioritization, and collaboration skills, with the ability to work effectively with technical and business stakeholders in a hybrid environment.
Experience in financial services, pension management, investment management, and capital markets is desirable.
Relevant Microsoft Power BI, Fabric, Azure data engineering, Databricks, Snowflake, or Power Platform certification is an asset.

Chief Communications and Corporate Affairs Officer
Ontario Health is implementing one of the most significant health system transformations in Canada. Created in 2019 to connect and coordinate care across the province, the agency unites world-class expertise in clinical care, digital health, quality, and system planning. Guided by its values of
Integrity, Inspiration, Tenacity, Humility, and Care
, Ontario Health works with partners across hospitals, community services, mental health, home care, and more to deliver better health outcomes and experiences for every Ontarian.
To confidentially explore this opportunity, please email your resume, quoting the appropriate position title, to Judy Mandelman or Heather Spiegel, at
resumes@promeus.ca.
The Position
Ontario Health is seeking an accomplished, astute, and highly strategic executive to serve as its next Chief Communications and Corporate Affairs Officer. Reporting to the President and CEO and serving as a member of the Senior Leadership Team, the Chief Communications and Corporate Affairs Officer will provide enterprise leadership for Ontario Health communications, corporate and public affairs, and stakeholder, patient, and family engagement.
This is a highly influential role at the intersection of government, health system transformation, and enterprise leadership. As a trusted advisor to the President and CEO, Board Chair, and senior leaders, the Chief Communications and Corporate Affairs Officer will help shape Ontario Health’s strategic positioning, reputation, and relationships with government and the health system.
A central priority will be maintaining strong relationships with Ministers’ offices, Ministry leadership, and other senior government decision makers. The Chief Communications and Corporate Affairs Officer will bring executive judgment, anticipate emerging issues and sensitivities, and ensure Ontario Health remains closely aligned with government priorities and expectations.
The Chief Communications and Corporate Affairs Officer will also position communications as a driver and enabler of the Ontario Health strategic agenda. Through proactive planning and a clear cadence of communications, they will help ensure Ontario Health has a compelling story to share about its priorities, progress, and impact, both within the organization and with external stakeholders. The Communications and Corporate Affairs portfolio includes internal and external communications, media and issues management, digital communications, brand and reputation, and stakeholder, patient, and family engagement.
This is not simply a communications leadership role. It is an enterprise role for an executive who can navigate complexity, influence at the highest levels, and help advance Ontario Health’s mandate across government and the health system.
The Person
The ideal candidate is an accomplished senior executive with significant leadership experience in communications, corporate affairs, or public affairs within government, the broader public sector, health care, or another complex and highly visible environment.
They bring deep experience working with elected officials and their teams, senior public servants, Boards, CEOs, and executive teams. They are recognized for sound judgment, discretion, and the ability to anticipate issues, navigate complex government environments, and build trust with senior decision makers.
An exceptional communicator and relationship builder, they can translate complex issues into compelling messages, build trust across diverse stakeholders, and operate effectively within a Crown agency environment. They combine strategic thinking with sound judgment and pragmatism and bring breadth and versatility to contribute beyond the traditional boundaries of a communications portfolio.

Directeur général des communications et des affaires internes
Santé Ontario met en œuvre l'une des transformations les plus importantes du système de santé au Canada. Créée en 2019 pour connecter et coordonner les soins dans toute la province, l'agence réunit une expertise de classe mondiale en soins cliniques, en santé numérique, en qualité et en planification du système. Guidée par ses valeurs que sont
l'intégrité, l'inspiration, la ténacité, l'humilité et la bienveillance
, Santé Ontario collabore avec des partenaires issus des hôpitaux, des services communautaires, de la santé mentale, des soins à domicile et d'autres secteurs afin d'améliorer les résultats et les expériences en matière de santé pour chaque Ontarien.
Afin d'explorer cette opportunité en toute confidentialité, veuillez envoyer votre CV par courriel, en indiquant le titre du poste approprié, à Judy Mandelman ou Heather Spiegel, à l'adresse
resumes@promeus.ca.
La position
Santé Ontario recherche un cadre expérimenté, avisé et doté d'un sens aigu de la stratégie pour occuper le poste de Directeur général des communications et des affaires internes. Rattaché(e) au Président-Directeur général et membre de l'équipe de direction, le Directeur général des communications et des affaires internes assurera la direction stratégique des activités de Santé Ontario en matière de communication, d'affaires internes et d'affaires publiques, ainsi que de l'engagement des intervenants, des patients et de leurs familles.
Il s'agit d'un poste très influent, à la croisée des domaines de l'action publique, de la transformation du système de santé et de la direction stratégique des activités. En tant que conseiller de confiance du Président-directeur général, du président du conseil d’administration et des hauts dirigeants, le Directeur général des communications et des affaires internes contribuera à définir le positionnement stratégique de Santé Ontario, sa réputation et ses relations avec le gouvernement et le système de santé.
L'une des principales priorités consistera à entretenir des relations solides avec les cabinets des ministres, les responsables des ministères et les autres hauts responsables gouvernementaux. Le Directeur général des communications et des affaires internes fera preuve d'un jugement de haut niveau, anticipera les enjeux émergents et les sujets sensibles, et veillera à ce que Santé Ontario reste en parfaite adéquation avec les priorités et les attentes du gouvernement.
Le Directeur général des communications et des affaires internes aura également pour mission de faire de la communication un moteur et un catalyseur du programme stratégique de Santé Ontario. Grâce à une planification proactive et à un rythme de communication bien défini, il contribuera à faire en sorte que Santé Ontario dispose d'un message convaincant à transmettre concernant ses priorités, ses progrès et son impact, tant au sein de l'organisation qu'auprès des intervenants externes. Le portefeuille du Directeur général des communications et des affaires internes comprend les communications internes et externes, les relations avec les médias et la gestion des enjeux, les communications numériques, la marque et la réputation, ainsi que l'engagement des intervenants, des patients et des familles.
Il ne s'agit pas simplement d'un poste de direction dans le domaine de la communication. Il s'agit d'un poste de direction destiné à un cadre supérieur capable de gérer la complexité, d'exercer une influence au plus haut niveau et de contribuer à faire progresser la mission de Santé Ontario au sein du gouvernement et du système de santé.
La personne
Le candidat idéal est un cadre supérieur chevronné, doté d'une solide expérience en matière de direction dans les domaines de la communication, des affaires internes ou des affaires publiques, acquise au sein du gouvernement, du secteur public au sens large, du secteur de la santé ou dans tout autre environnement complexe et très exposé aux regards du public.
Il possède une grande expérience de la collaboration avec les élus et leurs équipes, les hauts fonctionnaires, les conseils d'administration, les PDG et les équipes de direction. Il est reconnu pour son bon jugement, sa discrétion et sa capacité à anticiper les problèmes, à évoluer dans des environnements administratifs complexes et à instaurer un climat de confiance avec les hauts responsables.
Doté d'un talent exceptionnel pour la communication et la création de liens, il est capable de traduire des enjeux complexes en messages convaincants, d'instaurer un climat de confiance entre des intervenants divers et de travailler efficacement au sein d'un organisme public. Il allie réflexion stratégique, bon sens et pragmatisme, et apporte une vision large et une grande polyvalence qui lui permettent d'aller au-delà des limites traditionnelles d'un portefeuille de communication.

title: Lead, Capacity, Access & Flow
description:
Responsable, Capacité, accès aux soins et flux des patients
À Santé Ontario, nous sommes résolus à bâtir une solide culture organisationnelle qui unifie et responsabilise tous les membres de notre équipe à travers la province. Notre vision est qu'ensemble, nous serons des responsables en matière de santé et de bien-être pour tous. Notre mission est d'interconnecter le système de santé afin de favoriser l'amélioration et l'équité des résultats, des expériences et de la valeur en matière de santé. Notre façon de travailler ensemble se reflète dans nos cinq valeurs, l'intégrité, l'inspiration, la ténacité, l'humilité et l'attention.
Ce que Santé Ontario offre:
Chez Santé Ontario, votre croissance et votre bien-être ne sont pas seulement soutenus, ils sont célébrés à chaque étape. Ici, vous avez l'opportunité d'avoir un impact significatif tout en construisant une carrière épanouissante et durable. En fonction du poste que vous occupez, vous pourriez avoir droit
Une couverture santé complète dès le premier jour,
avec des prestations médicales, dentaires et optiques entièrement prises en charge pour vous et votre famille
Des comptes de dépenses flexibles pour les soins de santé ou le bien-être,
ainsi qu'un programme inclusif pour soutenir votre bien-être.

assurant une sécurité financière à long terme
Un droit à des congés compétitifs
qui donnent le temps de se ressourcer
Trois jours personnels et deux jours flottants par an
, offrant ainsi une flexibilité favorisant l'équilibre entre vie professionnelle et vie personnelle, en plus des jours de congés
Des opportunités de formation continue et de développement de carrière
conçues pour vous aider à progresser, à évoluer et à vous épanouir dans votre profession.
Un environnement de travail collaboratif et axé sur les valeurs,
où l'intégrité, la bienveillance, l'humilité, l'inspiration et la ténacité façonnent tout ce que nous faisons.
Des possibilités de participer à des communautés inclusives –
favorisant le sentiment d’appartenance, l’équité et le partage de perspectives diverses au sein de notre équipe
Voulez-vous faire la différence dans votre carrière?  Examinez l'opportunité qui s'offre à vous.
Relevant du directeur, Capacité, accès aux soins et flux des patients, le responsable fait progresser les stratégies régionales visant à améliorer la capacité du système de santé, l'accès, le flux des patients et les résultats liés aux autres niveaux de soins (ANS) à Toronto.
Dans le cadre de ses fonctions, le titulaire collabore avec des dirigeants cliniques et administratifs ainsi qu'avec des équipes transversales afin de renforcer la performance et les activités du système de santé dans l'ensemble de la région de Toronto.
Il s'agit d'un rôle régional axé sur l'évolution des besoins et des priorités de la région de Toronto.
Voici ce que vous aurez à faire :
Planification et amélioration du système de santé
Analyser les données régionales, les commentaires de la communauté et les pratiques exemplaires afin de cerner les lacunes du système, les priorités et les possibilités d'amélioration.
Diriger des initiatives régionales et des plans d'action éclairés par les données afin d'améliorer l'accès, le flux des patients et les résultats liés aux ANS.
Planification de la capacité du système
Surveiller la performance régionale en matière d'accès et de flux, cerner les tendances et les lacunes et soutenir les plans de capacité à court et à long terme qui favorisent le flux des patients.
Établissement et gestion des relations avec les intervenants
Établir des relations de confiance avec les fournisseurs de services de santé, les partenaires provinciaux et régionaux et les équipes internes afin d'harmoniser les priorités et de faire progresser les objectifs communs du système.
Fournir des conseils stratégiques et diriger des comités, des groupes de travail et des discussions avec les intervenants concernant l'accès, le flux et l'amélioration du système.
Gestion et réalisation de projets
Diriger des initiatives complexes et de grande envergure tout au long du cycle de vie des projets, en établissant des plans de travail, des jalons, les risques, la gouvernance et les outils de réalisation.
Coordonner les ressources internes et externes, harmoniser les processus de planification et communiquer les progrès aux partenaires et aux dirigeants principaux.
Gestion des enjeux et des intervenants
Anticiper et résoudre les enjeux complexes, élaborer des solutions pratiques et faciliter l'harmonisation entre les partenaires et les intervenants.
Cerner les possibilités de partenariat qui font progresser les priorités et les initiatives de Santé Ontario Toronto.
Ce dont vous aurez besoin pour réussir :
Formation et expérience
Diplôme universitaire en administration de la santé, en soins de santé, en administration des affaires ou dans un domaine connexe; une maîtrise est privilégiée. Une combinaison équivalente de formation et d'expérience sera prise en considération.
Au moins cinq années d'expérience dans un milieu de soins de santé.
Expérience en analyse de données, assortie d'un solide sens des finances.
Excellentes compétences informatiques, notamment dans l'utilisation de Microsoft Word, Excel, PowerPoint et SharePoint.
Capacité démontrée à établir, à renforcer et à maintenir des relations stratégiques avec les cliniciens, les gouvernements locaux et provincial, les fournisseurs de services de santé et d'autres intervenants clés, ainsi qu'à travailler efficacement au sein d'équipes diversifiées.
Connaissances et compétences
Solide compréhension du système de soins de santé et du continuum de soins, notamment des processus cliniques, de l'accès et du flux à l'échelle régionale ainsi que de leurs interactions avec les intervenants du système.
Bonne connaissance des ressources communautaires, notamment des services et des programmes; des rôles des professionnels de la santé; des milieux et des politiques hospitaliers; ainsi que des priorités, des enjeux et de l'évolution actuelle du système de soins de santé de l'Ontario.
Capacité démontrée à appliquer des méthodes de planification et d'analyse, à recueillir, à analyser de façon critique et à synthétiser des données et des renseignements provenant de multiples sources, ainsi qu'à formuler des recommandations efficaces fondées sur des données probantes qui soutiennent la planification et l'amélioration des soins de santé.
Esprit stratégique et systémique, capable de traduire des objectifs généraux en plans stratégiques et opérationnels détaillés.
Solides compétences en résolution de problèmes et en prise de décisions, avec la capacité d'analyser des problèmes complexes, d'interpréter les besoins opérationnels et cliniques et d'élaborer des solutions intégrées et créatives.
Grand sens de l'initiative et de l'autonomie, avec la capacité de travailler de façon autonome et en collaboration avec divers membres du personnel et intervenants.
Solides compétences en consultation, en négociation, en influence, en animation, en établissement de relations et en présentation.
Excellentes aptitudes en communication écrite, orale et interpersonnelle ainsi qu'en animation, avec la capacité de communiquer efficacement avec divers intervenants et dirigeants principaux dans l'ensemble du continuum de soins.
Compétences exceptionnelles en gestion de projets et expérience de la direction simultanée de plusieurs projets transversaux, de la planification et de l'élaboration jusqu'à la mise en œuvre.
Solides compétences en organisation et en gestion du temps, avec la capacité de réussir dans un environnement caractérisé par l'ambiguïté et la pression.

Patient Ombudsman's
role is to help resolve complaints from patients, residents and caregivers about their experiences in Ontario’s public hospitals, long-term care homes, home care services, and community surgical and diagnostic centres. Patient Ombudsman also investigates matters of public interest. We take the time to listen closely to all perspectives without taking sides. Our work aims to improve the system for everyone by shining a light on issues of concern. In accordance with ombuds principles, Patient Ombudsman acts independently of Ontario Health when undertaking its mandate, and we are committed to our values of respect, compassion, integrity and accountability. We do our work in service to a vision of a healthcare system where everyone is treated fairly.
What Patient Ombudsman offers:
At Patient Ombudsman, your growth and well-being aren’t just supported—they’re celebrated every step of the way. Here, you have the opportunity to make a meaningful impact while shaping a fulfilling and sustainable career. Based on your role, you may receive:
Comprehensive health coverage from day one

, fostering belonging, equity, and the sharing of diverse perspectives across our team
Want to make a difference in your career?  Consider this opportunity.
Reporting to the Manager, Investigations, the Investigator leads fair, thorough and timely investigations into complaints involving Ontario health sector organizations. Managing both individual and systemic matters, the role develops investigation plans, gathers and analyzes evidence, conducts interviews and inspections, and prepares clear, objective reports with well-reasoned findings and recommendations.
Here is what you will be doing:
Investigations
Manage a varied caseload of sensitive, high-profile and time-critical individual and systemic investigations, balancing timeliness, fairness and attention to detail.
Assess complaints and case files, identify key issues and risks, and develop proportionate investigation plans, methodologies and lines of inquiry.
Gather, review and analyze relevant records and evidence; plan and conduct interviews, site visits and inspections with complainants, witnesses and health sector organization staff.
Identify barriers to effective investigations, recommend practical solutions, and consult with the Manager and colleagues on strategy, resolution and escalation.
Share investigative expertise through file reviews, quality-improvement activities and support to Early Resolution Specialists.
Analysis and Report Writing
Evaluate evidence and relevant legal or regulatory considerations to develop impartial findings, recommendations and next steps.
Maintain complete, accurate and objective investigation records in the case management system.
Prepare clear, persuasive and accessible reports and correspondence that present the facts, analysis and evidence-based conclusions.
Communication
Use active listening, sound judgment and advanced interviewing skills to obtain relevant information and navigate sensitive or emotionally charged situations.
Communicate clearly, respectfully and professionally with complainants, health sector organizations, witnesses and other stakeholders across written, virtual, telephone and in-person channels.
Collaborate with the Patient Ombudsman team, provide timely case updates, flag emerging challenges and seek guidance as needed.
Compliance
Conduct work in accordance with applicable legislation, including the
Excellent Care for All Act
,
Freedom of Information and Protection of Privacy Act
,
Ontario Human Rights Code
,
Health Care Consent Act
and
Occupational Health and Safety Act
, as well as Patient Ombudsman policies and procedures.
Other Activities
Protect personal and personal health information and maintain strict confidentiality.
Contribute to learning, committees and special projects; coach colleagues and provide backup support to Early Resolution Specialists, as required.
Perform other duties as assigned.
Here is what you will need to be successful:
Education and Experience
Post-secondary degree in health administration, public administration, law, alternative dispute resolution or a related field, or an acceptable combination of education and experience.
A minimum of five (5) years of current experience conducting investigations in a similar type of organization, with proven experience in investigations and/or administrative oversight.
A minimum of five (5) years of current experience working with case management or information management systems.
Knowledge and Skills
Knowledge of Ontario’s public hospitals, long-term care facilities and/or home care sector.
Proven ability to understand and interpret legislation, policies and procedures, with knowledge of administrative law, ombudsman investigations, relevant case law, the rules of natural justice, due process, and procedural and substantive fairness.
Demonstrated ability to exercise sound judgment and integrity, remain independent and impartial, and analyze and identify issues without injecting opinion or acting as an advocate.
Demonstrated experience in mediation and alternative dispute resolution, including effective problem-solving and facilitating resolutions.
Demonstrated experience developing and executing investigation plans, supported by strong research and analytical skills to assess evidentiary relevance, identify risks and take appropriate steps to mitigate them.
Proven ability to interview individuals at all organizational levels, using strong interpersonal skills and discretion to manage and diffuse emotionally charged situations.
Excellent oral and written communication skills, with a demonstrated commitment to customer service and quality service delivery and the ability to work with and respond effectively to a diverse population.
Self-starter with the ability to work independently and collaboratively, maintain effective professional working relationships, and manage multiple priorities while completing investigations quickly without compromising quality or objectivity.
Proficient in Microsoft Office, case and information management systems, and office technologies.
Valid Class “G” driver’s licence and demonstrated ability to drive a motor vehicle.
Ability to travel to conduct interviews, gather evidence and complete inspections, and to attend meetings, events, training or conferences; occasional overnight travel is required.
Ability to attend public hospitals, long-term care facilities and private homes to conduct interviews and inspections, including working independently and interacting with vulnerable people. Investigators must provide a Vulnerable Sector Police Reference Check within sixty (60) days of employment.

Une couverture santé complète dès le premier jour,

Un environnement de travail collaboratif et axé sur les valeurs,

Des possibilités de participer à des communautés inclusives –

Voulez-vous faire la différence dans votre carrière?  Examinez l'opportunité qui s'offre à vous.
Santé Ontario recherche un(e) adjoint(e) administratif(ve) proactif(ve) et très organisé(e) pour fournir un soutien fiable aux directeurs, aux gestionnaires et à leurs équipes. Dans ce rôle, vous contribuerez à faire avancer les priorités en coordonnant les réunions, en gérant les documents et les sites SharePoint, en soutenant les activités d'intégration, en préparant le matériel et en assurant un suivi en temps opportun sur un éventail de projets et de programmes. Il s'agit d'une opportunité pour un professionnel rigoureux et attentif aux détails, qui s'épanouit dans un environnement dynamique, tisse des relations solides et est fier de permettre aux équipes de travailler efficacement.
Veuillez noter que ce poste revêt un caractère régional et répond aux besoins de la région Est.
Voici ce que vous aurez à faire :
Fournir un soutien administratif au quotidien, notamment la gestion de l'agenda, l'organisation des réunions, la préparation des déplacements, le traitement des notes de frais et la coordination des ressources du bureau.
Préparer, relire, compiler et tenir à jour les documents, présentations, graphiques, plans de projet, dossiers, systèmes de classement et le contenu SharePoint.
Coordonner les réunions de division et d'équipe en rassemblant les points à l'ordre du jour, en préparant le matériel, en rédigeant les comptes rendus, en assurant le suivi des actions et en garantissant un suivi en temps opportun.
Recevoir, évaluer, prioriser et répondre aux demandes de renseignements, aux correspondances et au courrier entrant, internes et externes, en signalant les problèmes aux niveaux supérieurs le cas échéant.
Favoriser une collaboration efficace avec les parties prenantes internes et externes en partageant l'information, en résolvant les problèmes et en aidant les équipes à rester organisées et alignées.

Ce dont vous aurez besoin pour réussir :
Formation et expérience
Diplôme de fin d'études secondaires ou supérieures en gestion administrative, en gestion d'entreprise, en commerce ou équivalent reconnu.
Environ deux ans d'expérience avérée dans le domaine administratif ou dans le soutien à des programmes, notamment en matière de coordination de tâches, de gestion de l'information et d'assistance à un responsable, à une équipe ou à un programme; des combinaisons équivalentes de formation, d'expérience et de diplômes peuvent être prises en compte.
Connaissances et compétences
Capacité avérée à travailler efficacement sous pression, à faire preuve de bon sens et à réagir avec professionnalisme face à des situations difficiles.
Solides compétences en matière d'analyse, de recherche et de résolution de problèmes, ainsi que la capacité à synthétiser et à présenter clairement des informations.
Expérience en matière de soutien administratif complet à un responsable, une équipe ou un programme, notamment grâce à l'utilisation de Microsoft Word, Excel, PowerPoint, SharePoint, Teams et du matériel de bureau standard.
Excellentes compétences en matière d'organisation et de gestion du temps, avec la capacité de gérer des priorités concurrentes.
Excellentes aptitudes relationnelles, de service à la clientèle et de communication, avec une approche professionnelle et réactive.
Permis de conduire valide et accès à un véhicule, car des déplacements occasionnels peuvent être nécessaires pour les activités de SO Est.

The Position
Reporting to the President and Chief Executive Officer, the Chief Regional Officer (CRO) for the Toronto and East Regions leads one of Ontario Health’s most complex and diverse portfolios. This region spans major urban academic centres and regional hospitals to small rural providers, as well as a diverse network of community-based services. The CRO is a visible and trusted system leader, accountable for translating provincial priorities into action, advancing regional integration, and ensuring consistent, high-quality, and measurable results across a challenging and dynamic environment.
Internally, the CRO will work closely with Ontario Health’s senior leadership team to align people, resources, and strategy, building team cohesion, strengthening operational capacity, and fostering a culture of collaboration and high performance. Externally, the CRO will represent Ontario Health with health service providers, Ministry officials, community leaders, and political stakeholders, cultivating trust-based relationships and navigating complex issues with clarity and integrity.
The CRO will provide credible, solution-focused leadership to help providers navigate workforce shortages, financial pressures, and infrastructure challenges while maintaining alignment with provincial standards. They will strengthen integration and planning across sectors, using data, relationships, and funding levers to improve access, continuity, and efficiency of care. Accountable for delivering on provincial performance targets that directly affect patient care and system sustainability, the CRO will monitor progress, act on emerging issues, and ensure measurable results. In a politically complex environment, they will build strong, respectful relationships with a wide range of stakeholders, addressing sensitive matters with diplomacy and transparency. At the same time, they will lead long-term system transformation, ensuring that immediate operational successes lay the foundation for a forward-looking vision of regional health system improvement.
This is an exceptional opportunity to shape system performance and integration in a region that reflects the full diversity of Ontario’s health landscape. The incoming CRO will guide the regions through ongoing operational pressures, while keeping a clear focus on long-term transformation and equity.
The Person
The ideal candidate is an accomplished health system leader with senior-level experience in health care service delivery, operational and financial administration, performance management, and/or data analytics. Adept at navigating complex, multi-stakeholder environments, they bring strong political acumen and a proven ability to work effectively with government, service providers, boards, and community stakeholders. They possess deep knowledge of Ontario’s health sector, including funding models, policy directions, and transformation priorities, and are skilled at turning strategic vision into measurable results. A collaborative and values-driven leader, they build trust, foster alignment, and inspire teams toward shared goals. Resilient and grounded, they demonstrate sound judgment, thrive in complexity, and remain focused on improving care and equity for the people and communities of Ontario.
