resumes@promeus.ca.
La position
Relevant du président-directeur général, le directeur général régional (DGR) des régions de Toronto et de l'Est dirige l'un des portefeuilles les plus complexes et diversifiés de Santé Ontario. Cette région englobe aussi bien de grands centres universitaires urbains et des hôpitaux régionaux que de petits fournisseurs en milieu rural, ainsi qu'un réseau diversifié de services communautaires. Le DGR est un responsable reconnu et de confiance du système, chargé de traduire les priorités provinciales en actions, de faire progresser l'intégration régionale et de garantir des résultats cohérents, de haute qualité et mesurables dans un environnement difficile et dynamique.
En interne, le DGR travaillera en étroite collaboration avec l'équipe de haute direction de Santé Ontario afin d'harmoniser les personnes, les ressources et la stratégie, de renforcer la cohésion de l'équipe et la capacité opérationnelle et de favoriser une culture de collaboration et de haute performance. En externe, le DGR représente Santé Ontario auprès des fournisseurs de services de santé, des représentants du ministère, des dirigeants communautaires et des intervenants politiques, en cultivant des relations fondées sur la confiance et en abordant des questions complexes avec clarté et intégrité.
Le DGR assure une direction crédible et axée sur les solutions afin d'aider les fournisseurs à faire face aux pénuries de main-d'œuvre, aux pressions financières et aux défis liés aux infrastructures, tout en maintenant la conformité aux normes provinciales. Il renforcera l'intégration et la planification entre les secteurs, en utilisant les données, les relations et les leviers de financement afin d'améliorer l'accès, la continuité et l'efficacité des soins. Responsable de la réalisation des objectifs de performance provinciaux qui influent directement sur les soins aux patients et la viabilité du système, le DGR suit les progrès accomplis, prend des mesures pour régler les problèmes émergents et veille à l'obtention de résultats mesurables. Dans un environnement politiquement complexe, il établit des relations solides et respectueuses avec un large éventail d'intervenants, tout en abordant les questions sensibles avec diplomatie et transparence. Parallèlement, il coordonne la transformation à long terme du système, en veillant à ce que les succès opérationnels immédiats jettent les bases d'une vision prospective de l'amélioration du système de santé régional.
Il s'agit d'une occasion exceptionnelle de façonner la performance et l'intégration du système dans une région qui reflète toute la diversité du paysage de la santé en Ontario. Le nouveau DGR guidera les régions face aux pressions opérationnelles continues, tout en maintenant clairement le cap sur la transformation à long terme et l'équité.
La personne
Le candidat idéal est un responsable accompli du système de santé possédant une expérience de haut niveau dans la fourniture de services de soins de santé, l'administration opérationnelle et financière, la gestion du rendement et/ou l'analyse des données. Apte à évoluer dans des environnements complexes impliquant de multiples intervenants, il fait preuve d'un sens politique aigu et d'une capacité avérée à travailler efficacement avec les pouvoirs publics, les fournisseurs de services, les conseils d'administration et les intervenants communautaires. Il possède une connaissance approfondie du secteur de la santé de l'Ontario, notamment des modèles de financement, des orientations politiques et des priorités de transformation. Il est également capable de transformer la vision stratégique en résultats mesurables. En tant que responsable collaboratif et axé sur les valeurs, il instaure la confiance, favorise la coordination et motive les équipes à atteindre des objectifs communs. Résilient et pragmatique, il fait preuve d'un bon jugement, s'épanouit dans les situations complexes et reste concentré sur l'amélioration des soins et de l'équité pour la population et les communautés de l'Ontario.
Afin d'explorer cette opportunité en toute confidentialité, veuillez envoyer votre CV par courriel, en indiquant le titre du poste approprié, à Judy Mandelman ou Heather Spiegel, à l'adresse
resumes@promeus.ca.

title: Coordonnateur des services cliniques /Clinical Services Coordinator
description:
À Santé Ontario nous sommes résolus à bâtir une solide culture organisationnelle qui unifie et responsabilise tous les membres de notre équipe à travers la province. Notre vision est qu'ensemble, nous serons des responsables en matière de santé et de bien-être pour tous. Notre mission est d'interconnecter le système de santé afin de favoriser l'amélioration et l'équité des résultats, des expériences et de la valeur en matière de santé. Notre façon de travailler ensemble se reflète dans nos cinq valeurs, l'intégrité, l'inspiration, la ténacité, l'humilité et l'attention.
Envie de donner un nouveau souffle à votre carrière?  Saisissez cette opportunité!
Relève de :
Gestionnaire, Centre de ressources provincial – Organes
Classification :
Coordonnateur des services cliniques (FT)
Lieu de travail :
Basé au 483, rue Bay
Horaire :
Combinaison de quarts de 12 heures en semaine et la fin de semaine
Le Réseau Trillium pour le don de vie (RTDV), qui fait partie de Santé Ontario, est responsable de la coordination du don et de la transplantation d'organes et de tissus en Ontario. Notre mandat comprend la sensibilisation du public à l'importance du don d'organes et de tissus, la formation des professionnels de la santé et l'assurance d'un système de don et de transplantation sûr et efficace en Ontario. En collaborant étroitement avec nos intervenants et en favorisant le développement organisationnel et individuel, nous accordons une grande importance à l'honnêteté, à la confiance, au respect et à la compassion.
Nous sommes actuellement à la recherche d'un coordonnateur des services cliniques (CSC) permanent à temps plein hautement motivé et expérimenté. Le CSC fournira des services professionnels conformes à la mission et aux valeurs du RTDV. La personne retenue est passionnée par le don d'organes et de tissus et s'engage à atteindre trois objectifs fondamentaux :
1) permettre à chaque personne ou à son représentant légal de prendre une décision éclairée et en toute confiance concernant la possibilité du don; 2) veiller à ce que le processus de don soit une expérience significative et positive pour les proches du donneur ainsi que pour le personnel hospitalier et les autres intervenants; et
3) contribuer au maximum à l'obtention de résultats optimaux pour les patients recevant une greffe d'organe ou de tissu.
Ce poste offre une occasion unique de combiner les pratiques exemplaires et l'expertise clinique. À titre de ressource clé dans le domaine du don d'organes et de tissus, ce rôle offre une grande autonomie ainsi que l'occasion de collaborer et de créer des liens avec divers intervenants cliniques et non cliniques.
Nous offrons un programme complet d'orientation et de formation, ainsi qu'un soutien continu de l'équipe afin d'assurer votre réussite dans ce rôle, de même que des possibilités de perfectionnement pour votre carrière à long terme.
Voici ce que vous ferez :
Gérer les cas liés au processus de don, de l'orientation jusqu'au prélèvement d'organes
Travailler en collaboration avec les hôpitaux donneurs, les équipes de soins de santé, les programmes de transplantation, les banques de tissus, les transporteurs terrestres et aériens, les laboratoires et les autres membres du personnel du RTDV
Coordonner l'attribution des organes et les analyses nécessaires
Prendre des décisions critiques et veiller au respect des règlements de Santé Canada
Faciliter la logistique du prélèvement d'organes et organiser le transport de plusieurs équipes de prélèvement (chirurgiens, transport terrestre et aérien)
Répondre aux appels des hôpitaux référents, effectuer une évaluation préliminaire des antécédents du patient et déterminer toutes les options de don pertinentes
Collaborer avec l'équipe de soins de santé responsable afin d'élaborer des stratégies permettant d'intégrer les services du RTDV au plan de soins de fin de vie du patient et de sa famille
Fournir à l'équipe de soins de santé des recommandations initiales concernant la gestion du processus ou l'état physiologique du patient, selon le cas, jusqu'à l'intervention d'un Spécialiste, Don d'organes et de tissus
Consigner des notes de dossier complètes et exactes et saisir les renseignements clés dans le dossier électronique et la base de données personnalisée du RTDV
Agir à titre d'expert dans tous les aspects du don d'organes et de tissus
Promouvoir et soutenir les pratiques exemplaires en matière de don d'organes et de tissus
Travailler selon des quarts rotatifs de 12 heures dans un centre d'appels occupé fonctionnant 24 heures sur 24, 7 jours sur 7
Exécuter toute autre tâche requise
Ce dont vous aurez besoin pour réussir :
Formation et expérience
Diplôme en sciences infirmières ou baccalauréat en sciences infirmières
Inscription à titre d'IA auprès de l'Ordre des infirmières et infirmiers de l'Ontario obligatoire
Minimum d'un (1) an d'expérience en soins infirmiers en milieu de soins critiques, de préférence
Expérience en don d'organes ou en soins infirmiers en transplantation, de préférence
Présence au bureau requise pour tous les quarts de jour (semaine et fin de semaine) (sous réserve de modifications)
Connaissances et compétences
Excellente compréhension de la physiopathologie appliquée et des examens diagnostiques médicaux et d'imagerie, ainsi qu'une capacité à interpréter les résultats de laboratoire
Capacité à analyser de grandes quantités de renseignements cliniques, à les comprendre et à les interpréter, puis à les communiquer clairement aux intervenants internes et externes
Compétences en gestion des conflits et capacité d'influencer les autres grâce à l'expertise et à des arguments rationnels
Expérience en gestion/coordination de cas
Expérience dans un environnement dynamique où les délais sont critiques
Capacité à résoudre des problèmes dans des situations de haute pression et sensibles au facteur temps
Excellentes aptitudes en communication, tant à l'écrit qu'à l'oral
Solides compétences informatiques
Taux horaire :
36,05 $ à 51,60 $
Type d'emploi :
Permanent à temps plein
Lieu de travail :
Toronto, Ontario
Tous les candidats doivent résider en Ontario pour être considérés pour des postes au sein de Santé Ontario.

Santé Ontario est un employeur accessible et nous offrons des accommodements dans tous les aspects de l’emploi, y compris le processus de recrutement. Si vous avez besoin d’un accommodement lié à un handicap pour participer au processus de recrutement, veuillez envoyer un courriel à careers@ontariohealth.ca et un membre de l’équipe vous contactera dans les 48 heures.
Clinical Services Coordinator
Want to make a difference in your career?  Consider this opportunity!
Reporting to:
Manager, Provincial Resource Centre – Organ
Classification:
Clinical Services Coordinator (Full time)
Worksite:
Based out of 483 Bay Street
Schedule:
Combination of weekday and weekend 12-hour shifts
Trillium Gift of Life Network (TGLN), part of Ontario Health, is responsible for the coordination of organ and tissue donation and transplantation in Ontario. Our mandate includes increasing public awareness of the importance of organ and tissue donation, education of health care professionals, and ensuring a safe and effective donation and transplant system in Ontario. Working collaboratively with our stakeholders and fostering organizational and individual growth, we value honesty, trust, respect and compassion.
We are currently seeking a highly motivated, experienced
permanent full time
Clinical Services Coordinator (CSC). The CSC will provide professional services in a manner consistent with the mission and values of TGLN. The incumbent is passionate about organ and tissue donation, and dedicated to achieving three core objectives, including:
1) enabling every person or legal surrogate to make an informed and confident decision about the option of donation 2) ensuring the process of donation is a meaningful, positive experience for the donor’s loved ones as well as for hospital staff and other stakeholders, and
3) contributing maximally to the attainment of optimal outcomes for patients receiving an organ or tissue transplant
This role offers the unique opportunity to blend best practice with clinical expertise. As a key resource in organ and tissue donation, this role provides a great deal of autonomy and the opportunity to liaise and network with a variety of clinical and non-clinical stakeholders.
We provide an extensive orientation and training program as well as on-going team support to ensure that you are successful in your role as well as opportunities to grow your broader, long-term career.
Here is what you will be doing:
Case management of the donation process from referral to organ recovery
Works collaboratively with donor hospitals, health care teams, transplant programs, tissue banks, air and land transportation carriers, labs and other TGLN staff
Coordinates organ placement and any necessary testing
Responsible for making critical decisions and ensuring that Health Canada regulations are followed
Responsible for facilitating the logistics of organ recovery and arranges transportation for multiple recovery teams (surgeons, land and air transportation)
Responds to calls from referring hospitals, conducts a preliminary assessment of the patient’s history and identifies all relevant donation options
Collaborates with the attending health care team in developing strategies for integrating TGLN services into the end-of-life care plan for the patient and family
Offers health care team initial recommendations related to management of the process or of the patient’s physiologic status, as appropriate, until a Specialist, Organ and Tissue Donation is involved
Documents comprehensive and accurate case notes and enters key information into TGLN’s electronic chart and custom database
Acts as an expert resource in all aspects of organ and tissue donation
Promotes and supports organ and tissue donation best practices
Works 12-hour rotating shifts in a busy 24/7 call centre environment
Performs other duties as required
Here is what you will need to be successful:
Education and Experience
Nursing Diploma and/or Bachelor of Science in Nursing
Current RN registration with the College of Nurses of Ontario is required
A minimum of one (1) year of critical care nursing experience preferred
Organ donation or transplant nursing experience preferred
All day shifts (weekday and weekend) are required to work in office (subject to change)
Knowledge and Skills
Strong understanding of applied pathophysiology, medical diagnostic testing/imaging, and ability to interpret laboratory results
Must be able to sort through large amounts of clinical information, understand/interpret the information and re-communicate the information to internal and external stakeholders
Conflict management and an ability to influence through applying expertise/rational arguments
Experience in case management/coordination
Experience working in a fast-paced time sensitive environment
Ability to problem solve in high pressure, time sensitive situations
Excellent communication skills – both written and oral
Strong computer skills
Rate of Pay:
$36.05 – $51.60 per hour
Employment Type:
Permanent
Full time
Employment Location:
Toronto, Ontario

External Accounting Advisor

The Ontario Securities Commission (OSC) is the statutory body responsible for regulating Ontario’s capital markets in accordance with the mandate established in the provincial Securities Act and the Commodity Futures Act. The mandate of the OSC is to provide protection to investors from unfair, improper or fraudulent practices, to foster fair, efficient and competitive capital markets and confidence in the capital markets, to foster capital formation, and to contribute to the stability of the financial system and the reduction of systemic risk. This mandate is performed through policy, operational, and enforcement activities. The OSC also contributes to national and global securities regulation development.
We offer a diverse, fair, and flexible work environment and take pride in our challenging and rewarding work.
The Senior Litigation Counsel, General Counsel’s Department, litigates non-Enforcement Division matters on behalf of the Commission before the Capital Markets Tribunal and the courts, including appeals, interventions, civil proceedings, insolvency-related matters, public interest litigation, transactional proceedings, contested regulatory matters, and reviews of Director or SRO decisions.
The role also acts as instructing counsel, manages external counsel, and provides strategic litigation and risk-mitigation advice to the Executive, the Commission, and internal divisions.
Key Duties and Responsibilities
Litigation Proceedings
Conduct proceedings, appeals, and interventions before the Capital Markets Tribunal and the courts with minimal supervision.
Provide strategic litigation advice and act as primary liaison to the OSC’s Regulatory Operations departments, such as the Department of Mergers & Acquisitions, on contested matters.
Act as counsel, or manage external counsel, in litigation involving the Commission, including developing strategy, preparing materials and witnesses, responding to claims, and resolving matters where appropriate.
Provide legal opinions and recommendations to mitigate risk, address public interest issues, and obtain instructions on complex or unusual matters.
Act for the Commission or supervise external counsel in claims against the Commission and in the enforcement of monetary sanctions, including collections matters.
Provide strategic litigation advice to Commission divisions on contested matters, including advocacy and litigation support for freedom of information requests.
Legal Advice
Provide practical legal and strategic advice that balances legal risk, public interest considerations, and organizational needs.
Serve as a subject matter expert on litigation, administrative law, investigations, proceedings, hearings, reviews, appeals, and related risk-management issues.
Advise on novel or complex legal issues, complaints, internal investigations, and litigation risk.
Independently review matters, identify issues, and pursue efficient resolutions.
Assess potential Commission interventions and coordinate with other CSA jurisdictions where appropriate.
Mentoring
Mentor and develop less experienced legal staff and articling students.
Qualifications
LLB or JD and member in good standing with the Law Society of Ontario.
Minimum of 10 years of relevant litigation experience; securities litigation or prosecution experience is an asset.
Experience litigating civil matters; prior private practice experience is an asset.
Strong knowledge of securities litigation, civil procedure, evidence, administrative law, and the Canadian securities regulatory environment.
Superior written and oral advocacy, legal analysis, judgment, negotiation, and strategic thinking skills.
Strong project-management skills and ability to lead complex, multidisciplinary work with significant impact.
Strong coaching and mentoring skills.

Criminal Investigations and Prosecutions
team is recruiting for a

What will you do?

description:
Business Unit
Fixed Term (Fixed Term), Full time

The Ontario Securities Commission (OSC) is the statutory body responsible for regulating Ontario’s capital markets in accordance with the mandate established in the provincial Securities Act and the Commodity Futures Act. The mandate of the OSC is to provide protection to investors from unfair, improper or fraudulent practices, to foster fair, efficient and competitive capital markets and confidence in the capital markets, to foster capital formation, and to contribute to the stability of the financial system and the reduction of systemic risk. Senior Forensic Accountant
Enforcement Division
18-month Contract
The
Enforcement Division
of the Ontario Securities Commission delivers fair, vigorous, and timely enforcement responses to capital markets misconduct. The Enforcement Division investigates and litigates breaches of securities laws in Ontario.  Team members work closely with other securities regulators, self-regulatory organizations and law-enforcement agencies to enhance initiatives to fight misconduct.  A strong visible enforcement presence assists in protecting investors from unfair, improper or fraudulent practices, fosters fair, efficient and competitive capital markets, fosters capital formation, and contributes to the stability of the financial system and the reduction of systemic risk.
The Enforcement Division is recruiting a
Senior Forensic Accountant
(18-month Contract) to support the investigation of criminal activity with a focus on fraudulent and recidivist behaviour that harms retail investors. The successful candidate will play a key role in advancing the Division's efforts to bring more Enforcement cases before the courts, where offenders may face significant penalties, including jail terms.
What’s in it for you?
Be an integral part of a leading-edge team leveraging an innovative mix of traditional investigative techniques, data analytics, and open-source intelligence analysis to investigate and assist in the prosecution of complex cases of Securities Act and Criminal Code offences.
Work in a collaborative, progressive, and professionally diverse team.
Make a difference and have a meaningful impact on investors and participants in Ontario’s capital markets.
What will you do?
Participate in complex financial investigations from intake through conclusion, including assessing referrals, identifying investigative objectives, and developing investigative strategies that evolve as the case progresses.
Lead or participate in multi-disciplinary investigation teams, establish priorities, coordinate investigative activities, and drive the timely progression of investigative files.
Direct the forensic accounting aspects of investigations in collaboration with investigators, litigators, and external law enforcement partners.
Collect, review, and analyze complex financial and non-financial evidence, including banking records, accounting records, corporate documents, digital evidence, and witness testimony, in accordance with investigative and evidentiary best practices.
Identify financial schemes, asset flows, concealment methods, and indicators of fraud, market misconduct, or other criminal and regulatory offences, and recommend appropriate investigative approaches.
Prepare comprehensive forensic accounting analyses, financial reconstructions, timelines, transaction flow charts, and evidentiary summaries to support investigative findings and recommended regulatory or criminal proceedings.
Assess evidence and make well-supported recommendations regarding investigative outcomes, enforcement action, regulatory proceedings, or criminal charges, taking into account legal considerations, evidentiary issues, and potential defences.
Draft and review investigative and legal documentation, including affidavits, Informations to Obtain (ITOs), production order materials, witness statements, evidentiary summaries, reports, and other court or tribunal-related documents.
Work closely with litigators and prosecutors to support hearing and court preparation, including disclosure review, witness preparation, identification of evidentiary gaps, analysis of inconsistencies, and development of examination strategies.
Testify as a fact witness regarding forensic accounting analyses, financial transactions, investigative findings, and chronology of events in regulatory or criminal proceedings.
What do you need to be successful in this role?
Undergraduate degree and prescribed course content required for Chartered Professional Accountant (CPA) exams.
Membership in good standing with CPA Ontario or equivalent designation in another jurisdiction.
Master of Forensic Accounting (MFAcc), Certified in Financial Forensics (CFF), Certified Fraud Examiner (CFE), or equivalent experience.
8 to 10 years of relevant forensic accounting experience as a qualified CPA.
Strong project management skills and strategic thinking on large, complex files, with the ability to effectively manage investigative scope and deadlines by designing structured approaches based on experience.
Excellent communication skills with the ability to actively listen, probe, and interpret information, including in examining witnesses, and to present complex technical information orally and in writing in a coherent, concise, and persuasive manner.
Problem-solving skills with the ability to demonstrate professional skepticism, resourcefulness, and good business judgment.
A demonstrated understanding of the Canadian and international securities environment and securities law. Familiarity with criminal law and procedure is an asset.
Experience with fraud investigations and forensic accounting in the context of capital markets is an asset.
Knowledge of business processes and procedures, accounting standards and systems of internal control.
Experience with e-discovery software and other data analytics tools is an asset.
If you are the type of person who:
is passionate about making a difference and having a meaningful impact on investors and participants in Ontario’s capital markets;
desires the opportunity to investigate challenging issues and work on high-profile and complex cases; and
enjoys being part of a dynamic and flexible work environment with a collaborative, progressive, and professionally diverse team.

description:

The Ontario Securities Commission (OSC) is the statutory body responsible for regulating Ontario’s capital markets in accordance with the mandate established in the provincial Securities Act and the Commodity Futures Act. The mandate of the OSC is to provide protection to investors from unfair, improper or fraudulent practices, to foster fair, efficient and competitive capital markets and confidence in the capital markets, to foster capital formation, and to contribute to the stability of the financial system and the reduction of systemic risk. This mandate is performed through policy, operational, and enforcement activities. The OSC also contributes to national and global securities regulation development.
We offer a diverse, fair, and flexible work environment and take pride in our challenging and rewarding work.
Team Lead, Case Assessment & Disruption
Enforcement Division
12-month Contract
The
Enforcement Division
of the Ontario Securities Commission investigates and litigates breaches of securities law in Ontario. Team members work closely with other securities regulators, self-regulatory organizations, law enforcement agencies, and government partners to combat misconduct and enhance investor protection. A strong and visible enforcement presence helps protect investors from unfair, improper, or fraudulent practices, fosters fair, efficient, and competitive capital markets, supports capital formation, and contributes to the stability of the financial system.
The
Case Assessment & Disruption Team
operates in a fast-paced, results-oriented environment, conducting initial inquiries into potential breaches of securities law and identifying opportunities to proactively disrupt misconduct before significant investor harm occurs. The team assesses complaints, tips, whistleblower submissions, referrals, and other information received from the public, market participants, regulators, and law enforcement agencies. Through evidence gathering, legal analysis, intelligence development, and collaboration, the team evaluates the nature and extent of potential misconduct and determines the most appropriate regulatory response, including disruption, referral, investigation, resolution, or closure.
The Opportunity
Case Assessment & Disruption is recruiting a Team Lead to oversee complex assessments, intake operations, and proactive disruption activities involving potential securities misconduct and emerging enforcement risks.
Reporting to the Head of Case Assessment & Disruption and supporting the Manager, the Team Lead provides leadership, strategic direction, and operational oversight for the intake and assessment functions. The role ensures matters are effectively triaged, prioritized, and advanced, while supporting the work of a multidisciplinary team responsible for assessing allegations, evaluating evidence, identifying potential breaches of securities law, and recommending appropriate regulatory responses.
The Team Lead also leads proactive disruption initiatives aimed at reducing investor harm and protecting market integrity. This includes identifying emerging risks, developing and implementing strategies to deter misconduct and disrupt harmful activities, and monitoring and reporting on disruption outcomes and trends to support informed decision-making and continuous improvement.
As a senior member of the team, the Team Lead plays a key role in ensuring the Division effectively identifies, prioritizes, and minimizes risk, leverages disruption opportunities, and delivers timely, impactful outcomes in support of the OSC's mandate.
Lead Complex Assessments, Disruption Strategies, and Enforcement Responses
Lead the assessment of complex securities misconduct matters, including fraud, market abuse, misleading disclosure, crypto-related misconduct, and other emerging risks.
Direct assessment strategies, evaluate evidence, identify potential breaches of securities law, and determine appropriate regulatory and enforcement responses of assessment team members.
Identify and oversee disruption opportunities to prevent investor harm, address unlawful activity, and protect market integrity.
Make critical decisions regarding file prioritization, referrals, investigation steps, disruptions, and closures, while promoting the effective use of data analytics, artificial intelligence, and emerging technologies to enhance assessment outcomes and operational effectiveness.
Provide Expert Regulatory Leadership and Operational Oversight
Serve as a subject matter expert in securities law, investigations, evidentiary standards, and enforcement practices, providing strategic advice to the team on complex matters.
Lead, mentor, and develop a multidisciplinary team while fostering a culture of excellence, accountability, collaboration, and continuous improvement.
Oversee matters from intake through assessment, ensuring file work is timely, risk-based, and compliant with legislative, policy, and procedural requirements.
Monitor team performance, capacity, outcomes, and operational risks, and report on results, emerging trends, and key performance metrics to support informed decision-making and continuous improvement.
Lead Strategic Partnerships and Continuous Improvement
Build and maintain relationships with regulators, law enforcement, government agencies, and other stakeholders to support enforcement and disruption objectives.
Lead information-sharing, deconfliction, and multi-agency initiatives involving regulatory, criminal, intelligence, and public-interest considerations.
Identify emerging risks, enforcement trends, and market developments and provide strategic advice to senior leadership.
Champion initiatives that enhance assessment effectiveness, disruption capabilities, operational efficiency, and enforcement outcomes.
What's In It For You?
Make a meaningful impact on investors and participants in Ontario's capital markets by helping identify misconduct and prevent investor harm.
Lead a highly specialized team responsible for some of the OSC's most complex, high-risk, and high-profile assessment and disruption matters.
Be at the forefront of innovative regulatory approaches that combine traditional investigative techniques, disruption strategies, data analytics, and collaboration.
Work in a collaborative, progressive, and professionally diverse environment alongside lawyers, investigators, forensic accountants, and specialists.
Influence regulatory outcomes and contribute directly to investor protection, market integrity, and public confidence in Ontario's capital markets.
What Do You Need To Be Successful In This Role?
Required Qualifications
Law Degree (LL.B. or J.D.) and membership in good standing with the Law Society of Ontario, or a CPA designation in good standing.
Minimum 10 years of progressive investigatory experience
in securities enforcement, regulatory investigations, financial crime investigations, regulatory compliance, or a comparable senior investigative role.
Demonstrated leadership experience leading, mentoring, coaching, and developing investigative or regulatory professionals.
Knowledge and Experience
Strong understanding of Ontario securities law, regulatory enforcement processes, and administrative proceedings.
Extensive knowledge of capital markets, investment products, registrants, market participants, and securities regulation.
Significant experience assessing complex allegations of misconduct and making evidence-based regulatory decisions.
Strong understanding of investigative methodologies, evidence collection practices, intelligence development, open-source intelligence techniques, eDiscovery processes, and data analytics.
Experience working with law enforcement agencies, regulators, self-regulatory organizations, government partners, and other stakeholders.
Experience handling complex, sensitive, and high-profile matters involving significant regulatory, legal, reputational, and operational risks.
Experience leading disruption initiatives, intelligence-sharing activities, and coordinated regulatory responses is considered a strong asset.
Leadership Competencies
Proven leadership, mentoring, and coaching abilities.
Strong project management experience overseeing multiple complex files, initiatives, or competing priorities.
Exceptional analytical thinking, problem-solving, and decision-making skills.
Ability to think critically, strategically, and creatively in a fast-paced and evolving environment.
Excellent judgment and ability to make sound decisions under pressure.
Outstanding written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to explain complex issues clearly and persuasively to staff, executives, regulators, and external stakeholders.
Strong interpersonal and stakeholder management skills with a demonstrated ability to build credibility and influence outcomes.
A collaborative leadership style and commitment to service excellence, accountability, and continuous improvement.

title: Practicum Student
employer: Public Health Ontario (Ontario Agency for Health Protection and Promotion)
description:
Practicum Student
Location: Toronto-661 University
Department: Scientist, Third Party Grants
This posting is to fill a current vacancy.
The Role:
The successful applicant will have the opportunity to contribute to two alcohol labelling research studies led by Dr. Erin Hobin. High-quality experimental evidence testing the effectiveness of alcohol labels on consumer outcomes is limited. To address this gap, Dr. Hobin is using novel research methods permitting experimental control in the field to estimate the impacts of alcohol warning labels on consumer knowledge and perceptions of alcohol health risks, and on alcohol use. This research responds to the policy priorities and evidence needs of Canadian and international decision-making bodies, including Health Canada and the World Health Organization. The successful applicant will have the opportunity to contribute to the research processes for two alcohol labelling studies.
The first study is a randomized field experiment to test the effects of different alcohol warning labels on consumer alcohol cognitions and on alcohol use. More than 1500 participants will be recruited from across the 10 provinces, randomized to 1 of 4 alcohol label conditions, and couriered a supply of labels according to their assigned label condition. Participants will be instructed to affix 1 label to all alcohol containers in their home over a 4-week period. Outcomes will be assessed at baseline and at 4 follow-up points using a brief online survey. Self-reported alcohol use will be corroborated using lipid biomarkers. The successful applicant will assist with coordinating the initial study administration planning, materials, and applications.
The second study is a pilot project assessing a standardized protocol for the self-collection of two dried blood spot samples from participants and testing the between-subject variability and inter-day precision of PEth levels as a biomarker of medium-term alcohol exposures as compared to self-reports of alcohol beverage consumption acquired by a series of weekly on-line surveys. Two sets of dried blood spots will be collected by participants over a 4 week period using a commercial dried blood spot collection device.
Please note:
•	This position is only open to students who are currently enrolled in an academic program where the completion of a practicum placement is required.
•	This position is only open to students currently residing in Ontario and attending a Canadian academic institution. Preference will be given to students enrolled in Ontario-based academic institutions.
•	This is a paid placement.
Suggested placement date: January to April 2027
Educational objectives:
• Support the collection, cleaning and management of primary data in one study.
• Apply data integrity checks and cleaning to primary datasets.
• Contribute to survey development and testing, including testing of survey logic and
refinement of participant-facing materials.
• Assist with study administration and recruitment planning.
• Provide participant support throughout the study, including responding to questions and
troubleshooting technical issues.
• Understand survey methods.
• Support primary data collection.
• Assist with study administration planning and materials.
• Opportunity to engage with public health practitioners and community leaders.
Proposed deliverables at the end of the placement:
•
Contribute to status and data reports for funding partners for the research.
• Contribute to development of data collection tools and surveys for the research.
• Oral presentation of the projects’ methods and results, delivered to a public health
audience.
Required education and experience:
•
Current enrollment in a Master of Public Health (MPH) program.
• Excellent Microsoft Excel skills.
• Excellent organizational skills.
• Strong oral and written communication skills.
• Knowledge of SAS or R (statistical software) considered an asset.
• Experience with REDCap or similar survey platforms considered an asset.
• Clear understanding of the research process acquired through practical or academic
experience considered an asset.

Coordonner, fournir des conseils en matière de traduction et d'intégration des services en français aux activités de Santé publique Ontario (SPO) et pour la livraison de produits et de services conformément aux exigences de la Loi sur les services en français (LSF).

Under the direction of the Team Lead, Production Development and Publishing, supports the implementation and execution of PHO's French Language Services (FLS) policy and strategy as well as supporting tools, training and resources including PHO managing translation requests, French-English lexicon, defining internal processes.
Manages the translation request process including the translation tracker and coordinates translation of PHO products and digital content with external service provides, ensuring compliance with Ontario Ministry of Government Services (MSG) procurement directives and guidelines; ensures all invoicing is accurate and complete.
Reviews and proofreads translated materials for quality assurance and liaises with vendors as required to enforce quality control.
Supports the development and ongoing content management of PHO's French language website and related digital content.
Provides expertise and support to internal program areas on FLS compliance and advises where PHO programs and policies may have an impact on the Francophone community.
Provides strategic advice, responses, issues management support, legislation interpretation and application on issues, trends, or complaints related to the provision of FLS.
Develops administrative processes, evaluation tools, performance measures and monitoring systems to monitor, track, evaluate and report PHO FLS requirements and activities and effectiveness of FLS implementation and compliance plans.
Supports manager in development and implementation of PHO operational policies, processes, best practices, tools and resources to promote compliance with FLS.
Develops, recommends and supports initiatives and special projects with direct impact on the Francophone community.
Acts as main point of contact for French Language Services clients

Provides training for PHO staff on all existing and any new French language polices and processes

Sous la direction du Responsable d’équipe, Développement de la Production et Publication, soutenir la mise en œuvre et l'application de la politique et de la stratégie sur les services en français de SPO ainsi que les outils, la formation et les ressources connexes, notamment la gestion des demandes de traduction et du lexique français-anglais et l'établissement des processus internes.

Soutenir la création et la gestion continue du contenu en français du site Web de SPO et du contenu numérique qui y est associé.
Offrir expertise et soutien aux secteurs des programmes internes relativement à la conformité en matière de services en français et fournir des conseils lorsque les programmes et les politiques de SPO peuvent avoir des répercussions sur la communauté francophone.
Offrir des conseils stratégiques, des réponses et du soutien en ce qui a trait à la gestion des enjeux, à l'interprétation et à l'application des lois touchant ces enjeux, aux tendances ou aux plaintes liées à la prestation de services en français.
Mettre au point des processus administratifs, des outils d'évaluation, des mesures de rendement et des mécanismes de surveillance, afin de contrôler, d'assurer le suivi, d'évaluer et de produire des rapports sur les exigences et les activités entourant les services en français à SPO et sur l'efficacité de la mise en œuvre des services en français et des plans de conformité.
Soutenir le/la gestionnaire pour l'établissement et la mise en œuvre de politiques opérationnelles, de processus, de pratiques exemplaires, d'outils et de ressources visant à favoriser la conformité aux services en français.
Créer, recommander et soutenir des initiatives et des projets spéciaux qui auront un effet direct sur la communauté francophone.
Agir comme principal point de contact auprès de la clientèle des services en français.
Assurer la liaison avec l'Office des affaires francophones provincial pour les enquêtes, les réponses et le traitement des plaintes concernant la prestation de services en français.
Offrir la formation nécessaire au personnel de SPO relativement à toute nouvelle politique ou tout nouveau processus en matière de langue française.
Soutenir le service des ressources humaines lors du recrutement en français afin que les politiques et procédures d'embauche respectent la LSF.
Knowledge and Skills-
Interpretive understanding of the FLSA and regulations in order to effectively coordinate the FLS function for PHO and provide expertise in the application of the FLSA to senior management.
Knowledge of Ontario's francophone community, issues and concerns.
Knowledge of health system in Ontario in order to support the development and implementation of French language products and help promote the role of PHO.

requirements, legislation and policies, to clarify processes or to de-designate, transfer or abolish designated positions.

employer: Public Health Ontario (Ontario Agency for Health Protection and Promotion)
description:
Compensation and Benefits Specialist
Location: Toronto-661 University
Department: HR Operational Services
This posting is to fill a current vacancy.
The Role:
The Compensation and Benefits Specialist provides expert analysis, advice, and operational support for PHO's compensation and benefits programs. The role is responsible for compensation administration, salary structure management, job evaluation, pay equity, benefits program oversight, market research, cost analysis, reporting, and continuous improvement. Leveraging organizational data, market intelligence, and industry best practices, the Specialist develops recommendations, business cases, and strategic advice to support compensation programs and organizational decision-making. The role serves as a key resource to leaders, managers, employees, and HR partners, and helps ensure compensation and benefits programs are competitive, sustainable, and aligned with legislative requirements, collective agreements, policies, and established practices.
Key Responsibilities -
Lead the annual compensation cycle, including merit increases, validation or approved of wage adjustments, and related implementation activities.
Administer salary structures and compensation programs in accordance with legislation, collective agreements, policies and approved practices.
Establishes and leverages relationships with external compensation partners, industry peers, and professional networks to obtain market insights, identify emerging trends, and support evidence-based compensation program design and decision-making.
Lead job evaluation for new and revised positions using the applicable methodology; document recommendations and support internal consistency and a defensible pay structure.
Maintain and support PHO’s pay equity program and related compliance requirements.
Provide data-driven advice on compensation matters and support the analysis and resolution of complex issues, including matters that may contribute to grievances.
Administer and support benefit program activities, including annual enrolment, plan changes, monthly remittances, escalated eligibility or coverage issues and employee appeals within the role’s scope.
Monitor benefit plan performance, cost, utilization, service quality and emerging market practices; identify risks and opportunities for improvement.
Monitor vendor performance against established service expectations and metrics and work with vendors and internal partners to resolve issues.
Support vendor reviews, procurement activities and implementation of approved benefit program changes.
Respond to or coordinate pension-related inquiries with the appropriate plan administrator and direct employees to the correct source for pension transactions, estimates or retirement advice.
Assess, interpret and provide guidance on compensation and benefits provisions in legislation, collective agreements, policies, procedures and plan documents.
Partner with HR Business Partners, HR leadership, managers and employees to provide clear, consistent and practical advice within the position’s area of responsibility.
Assess the impact of new legislation, collective agreements and approved program changes; develop and coordinate implementation plans to meet organizational obligations.
Recommend and implement improvements to compensation and benefits policies, programs, processes, templates and guidance tools to improve service and reduce organizational risk.
Maintain current knowledge of relevant legislation, regulations and industry practices.
Develop and prepare compensation and benefits reports, corporate statistics, costing and detailed analysis and scenario planning to support decision-making.
Use the HRIS and other tools to monitor data, validate approved position and employee information, investigate anomalies and support accurate reporting.
Partner with the HR Systems Advisor on system testing, implementation, maintenance, reporting and data integrity relating to compensation and benefits.
Liaise with Payroll on compensation and benefits matters to support accurate and timely pay and deductions.
Identify opportunities to improve or automate work through data, technology and streamlined processes.
Coordinate or lead special assigned HR projects and initiatives within the role’s scope, ensuring deliverables and timelines are met.
Develop clear communications, briefing notes, reports, tools and guidance materials for compensation and benefits programs and changes.
Deliver information sessions and explain complex requirements in language appropriate for employees, managers, senior leaders and HR colleagues.
Maintain effective working relationships with internal partners, benefit carriers, consultants, pension plan administrators, vendors and industry contacts.
Escalate material risks, exceptions and complex issues to the Manager, People Experience or other decision-makers, with analysis and recommended options.
Knowledge and Skills-
Working knowledge of legislation and regulatory requirements relevant to compensation and benefits.
Strong analytical and financial acumen, with the ability to interpret data, identify issues and provide practical recommendations.
Advanced proficiency with HRIS, reporting tools, spreadsheets, databases and word processing applications; ability to improve and automate processes using technology.
Excellent written and verbal communication, consultation, negotiation and customer service skills, including tact and diplomacy when handling complex or sensitive matters.
Ability to work independently, set priorities and manage multiple responsibilities and fixed deadlines in a fast-paced environment.
High attention to detail and sound judgment when working with confidential and sensitive information
Knowledge of artificial intelligence tools and emerging technologies, including the ability to use AI responsibly to support analysis, reporting, process improvement and service delivery.
Education and Experience-
Undergraduate degree in business, human resources or a related field, plus an accredited human resources program and at least seven years of related experience in a unionized environment, or an equivalent combination of education and experience.
Certified Compensation Professional (CCP) or in progress.
CHRP designation preferred
Advanced knowledge of compensation and benefits program design and administration, job evaluation, salary structures, market analysis, pay equity and collective agreement application.
Attributes and Competencies-
Provides authoritative advice and recommendations on compensation, benefits, job evaluation and related HR programs, often involving sensitive, complex or contentious issues.
Develops and delivers reports, presentations, briefing notes, communications materials, procedures and guidance documents used to support employee understanding and management decision-making.
Uses tact, diplomacy and influencing skills when communicating decisions, explaining program requirements, addressing concerns or resolving disputes where there may be disagreement or competing interests.
Builds and maintains productive working relationships with internal stakeholders, Payroll, HR Systems, benefits carriers, pension administrators, consultants and other external partners to facilitate effective service delivery.
Provides responsive, high-quality service by assessing client needs, researching issues and delivering accurate information, recommendations and solutions.
Ensures compensation and benefits programs are administered consistently, fairly and in accordance with legislation, policies, plan provisions and collective agreements.
Analyzes issues of varying complexity using legislation, collective agreements, policies, precedents, plan documents, market information and HRIS data.
Determines when an issue can be resolved within established authority and when options or recommendations must be escalated for decision.
Identifies and prioritizes time-sensitive compensation and benefits activities, anticipates data or process issues and initiates corrective action.
Provides subject matter expertise and practical guidance to HR colleagues, managers and senior leaders.

The Coordinator, Examination Accommodation and Delivery (“Coordinator”), under minimal supervision, is responsible for the delivery of specialized and individualized services to candidates

Human Rights Code
, R.S.O. 1990. c. H.19 and

The Coordinator specializes in an area of examination delivery e.g. paralegal or lawyer licensing examinations that may be situated in Toronto or four other Ontario cities. The Coordinator is responsible for the planning, staffing, and other business operations of delivering examinations, including the selection and contracting of venues and services required for large examination sittings, and providing appropriate training and supervision to large numbers of support personnel.

Minimum of college diploma in a related field with computer proficiency in Microsoft Office, Customer Relationship Management (CRM,) email, internet, and various hardware set ups.

Minimum of 5 years of experience in an event-delivery, customer-service, or administrative role within an education, regulatory, or medical environment, or the equivalent.
Ability to use initiative and work independently, and as a member of a dynamic and integrated service team.
Proven administrative and project management skills are required, preferably in a client-focused environment.

Demonstrated ability in the planning and delivery of client-focused administrative services and large scale, secure events in a regulatory, academic, or medical environment.
Knowledge of the Law Society’s mandate, services, organizational structure, rules, regulations, relevant legislation and policies, pertaining to the lawyer and paralegal licensing processes.
Demonstrated ability to recruit, train, and provide leadership to support personnel.

Job Purpose
The Director, Enterprise Planning & Performance will build and manage a small professional team and is charged with strengthening enterprise-wide planning, performance measurement, and transparent reporting on delivery of the Law Society’s Strategic Plan. Reporting to the Executive Director, Strategy, the Director supports the CEO, Executive Committee and Convocation by establishing practical planning rhythms, enterprise-level key performance indicators (KPIs), and disciplined reporting that demonstrates progress against approved strategic objectives in a manner that is clear, transparent and measurable.
The Director works in partnership with operational areas across the organization as well as Business Innovation and Operations Management (BIOM), Information Technology (IT) and Finance as an enterprise integrator, helping to connect priorities, surface interdependencies, and support coordinated execution of the Strategic Plan. Working through influence, the Director helps ensure that planning and reporting processes are coherent, proportionate and supportive of effective delivery.
Key Accountabilities:
1. Enterprise Planning & Performance Framework (Planning)
Under the guidance of the Executive Director, Strategy, the Director provides leadership and expertise to the CEO, Executive Committee, and Convocation to achieve the Law Society’s objectives with respect to enterprise planning, execution discipline, and performance accountability. Establishes and maintains enterprise planning cycles, templates and routines that translate approved strategic priorities into clear initiatives, milestones and measurable outcomes. Supports enterprise prioritization, sequencing and trade-off decisions across initiatives and resources.
2. Enterprise Planning & Accountability Reporting (Delivery)
Coordinates the development, implementation, monitoring and reporting of enterprise-level performance measures and progress against the Strategic Plan, supporting the CEO’s and Executive Committee’s accountability to the Board through clear and measurable reporting. Defines reporting standards to ensure that Strategic Plan accountability is evidence-based, reliable, and consistent over time.
Works in partnership with leaders and teams across the organization as an enterprise integrator to coordinate cross-functional inputs into KPI dashboards, progress updates, and briefing materials that reflect organizational outcomes achieved, delivery risks, mitigation actions, dependencies, and overall confidence in execution of the Strategic Plan. This includes but is not limited to coordination with Policy, Professional Development & Competence, Professional Regulation, Finance, Business Innovation & Operations Management, Information Technology, Communications and others.
3. People Leadership
This senior position supports the Executive Director in ensuring that deliverables will be appropriately operationalized, and that day-to-day mentoring and direction are provided.
Hires, trains, develops and evaluates employees accountable to the Director in accordance with organizational policies and best human resources practices. Fosters a team environment by role modeling leadership behaviour, empowering employees accountable to the Director and building team capability.
4. Financial Responsibility
Assists the Executive Director with developing and monitoring the team’s budget and project-related expenditures, adjusting plans as required to meet fiscal resource constraints.
5. Team Membership
Able to work collaboratively in supporting the CEO, the Executive Committee, and senior leaders, ensuring consistency in enterprise planning and performance reporting across the organization. Works with various internal stakeholders and cross-functional teams, providing leadership and expertise to team members, ensuring broad information and idea exchange.
The Director demonstrates personal excellence, bringing knowledge and functional expertise to the team. Contributes to group decision-making and processes, generating ideas that are strategically sound, integrated with the Law Society’s broader mandate, and achievable in a timely, balanced and fiscally sound manner.
6. Relationship and Alliance Building
Builds credibility and develops effective working relationships with key groups both internally and externally. Partners with operational leaders to support coordination without undermining operational authority. Works closely with Professional Development & Competence and Professional Regulation divisions to understand the core functions of the organization. Where appropriate, supports strategic relationships and shared learning with other regulatory bodies or sector partners on planning, performance measurement and modernization approaches.
Qualifications
Education
The minimum level of education required to fulfill the core requirements of this position includes a university degree in Business Administration, Public Administration, Public Policy, Law or a related field. An equivalent combination of education and experience may be considered.
Experience
The position requires a minimum of 10 years’ progressive related experience gained in a complex, multi-stakeholder environment such as a government, regulatory or complex not-for-profit environment, at least 5 of which are in a managerial / leadership capacity.
Function Related Skills, Knowledge and Abilities
Comprehensive understanding of enterprise planning, performance measurement and reporting in a complex organization, including governance and accountability expectations.
Demonstrated ability to translate strategic priorities into measurable outcomes, performance indicators, and practical reporting products.
Proven ability to synthesize complex information quickly and communicate it clearly in concise, well-written reports and briefings.
Strong facilitation and relationship management skills; ability to influence without authority and coordinate across functions.
Experience working in highly political situations, managing a variety of viewpoints and sensitivities.
Political astuteness and sound judgment to calibrate intervention—staying light-touch where work is on track and increasing support where delivery is at risk.
Capability to lead, develop and manage a team of professionals, including the conducting of annual team member performance reviews.
Demonstrated ability to assess organizational capability and adjust plans as required to successfully carry out organizational strategies.
Demonstrated ability to manage multiple agendas, meet changing deadlines, and deliver on a large number of concurrent commitments.
Superior analytical and communication skills coupled with excellent interpersonal and negotiation skills.
Technical Skills and Knowledge
Computer literacy, including familiarity with email, word processing, spreadsheets, databases and dashboards.
Ability to partner effectively with BIOM/IT on data definitions, reporting automation and CRM-enabled insights.

description:
About Us
The Ontario Cannabis Store provides safe, responsible access to recreational cannabis for adults 19 and older. We operate the sole legal online store for recreational cannabis in Ontario and are the provincial wholesaler of cannabis for private retail stores.
Working at the OCS is a unique opportunity to be part of an agile start-up in a ground-breaking new industry.  We’re a diverse team passionate about delivering a great customer experience, working together with mutual respect and building value out of our differences.  We’re an inclusive organization that understands that delivering great results comes out of ensuring every voice is heard.
About the Role
We're looking for a Senior Systems Analyst to join our team.
The Senior Systems Analyst serves as the lead analyst and solution design specialist for enterprise technology initiatives. Working within established architecture and solution direction, this role translates high-level designs into system-specific configurations, ensuring solutions are feasible, optimized, and aligned with business requirements. As a key subject matter expert and trusted partner to Architects, the Senior Systems Analyst brings deep system knowledge and technical expertise to support the successful delivery of enterprise solutions.
Acting as a subject matter expert throughout the solution lifecycle, the Senior Systems Analyst provides end-to-end solution analysis, influences solution decisions, drives design quality, and supports the successful delivery of complex, business-critical programs. This role also identifies and enables opportunities to leverage Artificial Intelligence (AI) and automation within enterprise systems to enhance process efficiency, improve decision-making, and elevate the user experience.
About Your Day
Analyze and translate business requirements into scalable system solutions aligned with enterprise architecture standards, roadmaps, and integration patterns.
Lead requirements gathering, solution design, impact assessments, and cross-functional workshops to define scope, resolve gaps, and identify risks, dependencies, and optimization opportunities.
Design and support enterprise platform configurations, integrations, data flows, and AI-enabled capabilities while ensuring scalability, governance, compliance, data quality, and alignment with business and technical requirements.
Provide technical leadership and guidance to project teams, promoting best practices, maintaining traceability across the delivery lifecycle, and supporting successful implementation and testing.
Act as a key liaison between business and technical stakeholders, influencing requirements, leading solution trade-off discussions, mentoring team members, and collaborating with vendors and partners to support delivery.
Serve as a subject matter expert for enterprise applications, digital commerce platforms, customer-facing portals, and Azure integration services, leading issue resolution, process optimization, automation, continuous improvement, and evaluation of emerging technologies, including AI/ML solutions.
About You
Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, or a related field (or an equivalent combination of education and experience); relevant certifications or experience with Digital Commerce Platforms, Microsoft Azure, or Enterprise Integration Technologies are considered an asset.
5–8 years of experience in a Systems Analyst, Functional Consultant, or similar IT role supporting digital commerce platforms, customer portals, web applications, and large-scale business-critical systems.
Experience with APIs, web services, middleware, enterprise integrations, relational databases, data analysis, and troubleshooting end-to-end business transactions across web and backend systems.
Strong understanding of digital order management and customer-facing business processes, including retailer onboarding, account management, catalog management, inventory visibility, ordering, fulfillment, invoicing, and claims.

location: 90 Wildcat Rd, North York, ON M3J 2V4, Canada
description:
About Toronto Community Housing Corporation
Toronto Community Housing Corporation (“TCHC”) is the largest social housing provider in Canada and the second largest in North America. We are wholly owned by the City of Toronto and operate in a non-profit manner. TCHC provides homes to over 41,000 low and moderate-income households in 88 of Toronto's neighbourhoods, with 93,000 tenants from many different backgrounds with a diversity in age, education, language, mental and physical ability, religion, ethnicity and race. We are an essential part of the City of Toronto's fabric and social system.
Our over 2,000 employees work to achieve our vision of quality homes in vibrant communities where people are proud to live and work.
Vacancy Type:
Full-time Permanent
Salary/Hourly Range:
$123,900.46 - $
148,680.56
Work Details (Days/Hours):
Monday – Friday 36.26 hours per week
Hybrid Eligible
Yes
Affiliation:
Non-Union: Management/Exempt
Division and Department
Community Safety Unit
Number of Vacancies:
One (1)
Existing/New Job:
Existing
Grade:
8
Vacancy Status
Existing
Candidate List or Eligibility List:
Candidate List
What we offer
In addition to competitive compensation and a rewarding career where you can truly make a difference, we offer a comprehensive package that meets the various needs of our diverse employees, including:
Ability to participate in inclusive employee-led networks to educate, inspire, amplify voices, build relationships and provide development opportunities;
Minimum four (4) weeks of paid annual vacation days, increasing with years of service;
Four (4) paid personal days;
Defined benefit pension plan with OMERS, includes 100-per-cent employer matching;
Health and dental benefits, including a health spending account available upon your start date;
Employee and family assistance program;
Maternity and parental leave top up (93% of base salary);
Training and development programs including tuition reimbursement of $1500 per calendar year.
Fitness membership discount;
This job offers the opportunity to work from home as part of a hybrid work arrangement. This arrangement will allow you to work some days at a TCHC work location and the rest of the time from home. The amount of time required to work at a TCHC work location is flexible, while considering operational and service delivery requirements.
Make a difference
Reporting to the Senior Director, Community Safety Unit, the Manager, CSWB Implementation and Project Management provides disciplined implementation, project-management and coordination leadership for Toronto Community Housing’s Community Safety and Well-Being (CSWB) Strategy. The position translates the Board-approved Strategy into sequenced workplans, coordinates place-based pilots and Community Safety and Well-Being Plans, supports integrated service tables, and ensures that commitments, risks, dependencies and implementation learning are tracked and acted upon.
The position works across CSU, Regional Operations and other TCHC divisions, as well as with tenants and external partners. It provides implementation governance and project discipline but does not exercise daily operational command, direct front-line deployment, independent quality assurance or corporate analytical ownership.
What you’ll do
CSWB Strategy Implementation and Portfolio Management
Translates the Board-approved CSWB Strategy and annual priorities into a multi-year implementation roadmap and detailed annual workplans.
Maintains the master implementation plan across the five CSWB outcome areas, including deliverables, milestones, accountable owners, dependencies and timelines.
Establishes and maintains a portfolio view of major CSU and cross-divisional projects to support prioritization, sequencing and management oversight.
Develops project charters, governance structures, work breakdowns, schedules, decision logs, risk and issue registers, and project-closure documentation.
Monitors implementation progress, tests the reliability of status updates and identifies delays, scope changes, unresolved decisions and capacity constraints.
Escalates material barriers and recommends practical corrective action, re-sequencing, resource adjustments or governance decisions.
Promotes consistent project-management methods while tailoring the level of documentation and control to the size, risk and complexity of each initiative.
Ensures implementation reflects TCHC’s strategic priorities, tenant-centred service commitments, equity obligations and approved CSWB principles.
Place-Based Pilots and Community Safety Planning
Leads the project management of East, Central and West CSWB pilots and any approved expansion to additional communities.
Coordinates development, implementation and periodic review of place-based Community Safety and Well-Being Plans.
Integrates operational information, tenant experience, community conditions, environmental findings, partner capacity and available analytical evidence into practical action plans.
Ensures each pilot or plan includes clearly defined outcomes, actions, owners, timelines, resources, measures and review points.
Maintains pilot-specific action, risk, issue and decision logs and ensures overdue or unresolved matters are addressed through the appropriate escalation route.
Documents implementation learning, identifies transferable practices and recommends adjustments to the operating model before broader expansion.
Develops and applies readiness, need, sustainability and capacity criteria when recommending whether and how CSWB planning should expand.
Integrated Service Coordination, Partnerships and Tenant Input
Establishes and supports integrated working tables for complex community safety and well-being priorities requiring coordinated action.
Coordinates participation from CSU, Regional Operations, Facilities, Tenancy Management, Programs and Partnerships, Communications and other relevant TCHC functions.
Supports structured involvement of external partners, including community organizations, health and social services, violence-prevention partners, emergency services and other public institutions.
Ensures meetings result in documented decisions, assigned actions, clear deadlines and appropriate follow-through rather than information-sharing alone.
Coordinates with corporate and regional engagement leads so that tenant priorities and lived experience inform local plans and implementation decisions.
Tracks commitments arising from tenant and partner engagement and supports timely communication back to tenants on progress and constraints.
Maintains role clarity between project coordination and the operational delivery responsibilities of Special Constables, Community Safety Advisors, investigators and other service teams.
Implementation Frameworks, Governance and Reporting
Designs and maintains implementation frameworks for cross-functional priorities, including the CSU call follow-up model and other approved service improvements.
Defines governance requirements, accountabilities, service expectations, escalation paths and closure criteria in consultation with functional owners.
Prepares concise implementation dashboards, status reports, briefing notes, presentations and decision materials for the Senior Director and senior management.
Supports preparation of ELT, Committee and Board reports by providing validated implementation status, risks, milestones, lessons and next steps.
Works with Research, Analytics and Performance to align implementation milestones with appropriate performance measures, baselines and evaluation plans.
Works with Records and Quality Assurance to ensure implementation controls, records and compliance requirements are incorporated into project design.
Maintains complete, accurate and accessible project records in accordance with TCHC records-management, privacy and information-security requirements.
Functional Leadership, Resource Stewardship and Continuous Improvement
Provides functional leadership and direction to employees, consultants, working groups and project teams assigned to CSWB implementation initiatives.
Builds cooperation among stakeholders with different mandates, priorities and operational pressures and facilitates resolution of implementation issues.
Develops project resource estimates and supports annual business planning, budget development, procurement and business-case preparation.
Monitors approved project expenditures, contracts and deliverables within delegated authority and promptly identifies variances or emerging pressures.
Identifies change-management, communication, policy, technology and training requirements needed for successful implementation and coordinates with the accountable functional leads.
Promotes an inclusive, respectful, trauma-informed and learning-oriented approach to project leadership and community safety planning.
Undertakes other related responsibilities and special projects assigned by the Senior Director.
