Make a difference
The Workplace Investigator is responsible for investigating allegations of employee misconduct, workplace harassment, discrimination, reprisal, violence, policy breaches, and other workplace concerns in accordance with TCHC policies, applicable collective agreements, legislation, and workplace investigation best practices. As part of the Employee and Labour Relations Team within People & Culture, the position conducts threshold assessments, develops investigation plans and terms of reference, identifies the scope and mandate of investigations, conducts fair and respectful interviews, gathers and assesses relevant evidence, analyzes applicable policy, collective agreement and legislative requirements, makes findings of fact on an objective and evidence-based basis, and prepares clear, thorough, neutral and well-supported investigation reports. The role carries out investigations in a timely, impartial, procedurally fair, confidential, trauma-informed and culturally responsive manner, applying an equity, anti-Black racism and human rights lens while maintaining neutrality and avoiding assumptions, bias or prejudgment.
What you’ll do
Investigation Intake, Planning and Execution
Supports and conducts assigned components of the workplace investigation process from complaint intake to conclusion, including triage, threshold assessment, scoping, investigation planning, interviews, evidence gathering, analysis, credibility assessment, findings and reporting for complex workplace issues, including harassment, discrimination, reprisal, inappropriate conduct, workplace violence and other alleged misconduct or breaches of TCHC policies, collective agreements or legislation. Applies a demonstrated understanding of anti-Black racism throughout the process, recognizing that it may be explicit or subtle and may arise through individual conduct, racial stereotypes, organizational culture, institutional practices, differential application of policies, or patterns of cumulative disadvantage.
Conducts research into assigned areas ensuring that such research takes into account developments within the field, corporate policies and practices, legislation and initiatives by other levels of government.
Investigates complex allegations of workplace misconduct or wrongdoing for unionized and non-unionized staff across the organization, including fraud, conflict of interest, theft, maladministration, harassment, discrimination, reprisal, nepotism, cronyism, substance-related concerns, unethical behaviour, workplace violence, breaches of workplace standards and other conduct concerns. Ensures allegations are reviewed and analyzed through a fair, neutral, timely, evidence-based and policy-grounded process, with attention to fact-finding, procedural fairness and detail.
Equity, Human Rights and Culturally Responsive Practice
Applies distinctions-based and culturally safe investigation approaches that respect First Nations, Métis and Inuit peoples by avoiding pan-Indigenous assumptions and supporting participant-led cultural or community supports where requested and appropriate.
Applies procedural fairness equitably rather than mechanically, recognizing that impartiality does not always require identical treatment of every participant. Identifies and appropriately addresses relevant barriers, accessibility requirements, cultural considerations, racialized power imbalances and participation needs while maintaining a neutral, confidential and evidence-based investigative mandate.
Exercises essential investigative skills, including critical thinking, active listening, trauma-informed interviewing, credibility assessment, data and document analysis, rigorous research methods, and effective time management to ensure investigations are thorough, impartial, unbiased, timely, well documented and capable of withstanding internal, arbitral, tribunal or court scrutiny.
Conducts credibility and reliability assessments without relying on racialized assumptions or stereotypes concerning demeanor, communication style, emotional expression, accent, tone, confidence, perceived professionalism, authority, cooperation or trustworthiness. Assesses testimony within the full factual, cultural, organizational and power context, while relying on relevant and probative evidence.
Applies trauma-informed, anti-racist, anti-oppressive, culturally responsive and human rights-informed approaches throughout workplace investigations, recognizing that participants may have different lived experiences, communication needs, accessibility needs, trauma histories or emotional responses, while maintaining investigator neutrality, procedural fairness and an evidence-based mandate.
Uses effective communication, accommodation-aware practices, psychological safety tools and respectful interview techniques to engage with persons of diverse identities, abilities, backgrounds and experiences, including individuals who may be distressed, distrustful, guarded, or have heightened emotional responses because of the alleged incident, disability, trauma, prior experience of discrimination, institutional distrust or systemic barriers.
Evidence Assessment, Reporting and Records
Conducts on-site and or virtual interviews and gathers evidence at various work locations.
Maintains accurate, complete and well-organized investigation records, including detailed interview notes, meeting minutes, documentary evidence, electronic and hardcopy records, chronology reports, file summaries, correspondence, disclosure materials and other investigation-related documentation. Ensures records are consistently labelled, securely maintained, readily retrievable, and managed in accordance with TCHC record-keeping practices, confidentiality requirements, privacy obligations and litigation or adjudicative needs.
Assesses the evidence, applies credibility analysis where required, and makes findings of fact based on the balance of probabilities, the applicable factual record, and relevant policies, procedures, collective agreement provisions or legislation. Prepares detailed reports, confidential communications and briefings that clearly distinguish facts, evidence, analysis, findings and any applicable policy conclusions.
Develops investigation plans, terms of reference, interview plans, evidence lists, findings reports and related communications with input from the Manager, Employee and Labour Relations, as appropriate, to ensure the investigation process is consistent, fair, well scoped, legally defensible, confidential and aligned with TCHC standards.
Stakeholder Communication and Proceedings
Works collaboratively with internal partners, management, union representatives where applicable, law enforcement agencies and legal counsel to exchange information on a need-to-know basis, preserve confidentiality, support procedural fairness, and ensure investigation-related communications are accurate, respectful and appropriately documented.
Testifies and gives evidence regarding workplace investigations in legal or adjudicative proceedings, including arbitration, Human Rights Tribunal of Ontario proceedings, criminal proceedings, civil litigation or other forums, as required.

Represents TCHC on corporate initiatives and committees related to investigations, respectful workplace, human rights, equity, health and safety, and other related matters.
Develops and delivers education, guidance and training on workplace investigation policies, procedures and best practices, including procedural fairness, confidentiality, trauma-informed interviewing, anti-racist and anti-oppressive practice, documentation standards, evidence handling, neutrality and the role of participants in the investigation process.
Models and contributes to an environment that supports equity, inclusion, dignity, respect, psychological safety and organizational change. Provides subject matter expertise and consultation to management and employees on rights, responsibilities, roles and expectations within the investigation process, while reinforcing procedural fairness, neutrality and confidentiality.
Maintains and applies advanced working knowledge of human rights, anti-racism and equity principles relevant to workplace investigations, including individual, interpersonal, systemic and institutional dimensions of anti-Black racism; racial stereotyping and coded language; intersectional discrimination; racial harassment; reprisal; accommodation; accessibility; anti-Indigenous racism; gender identity and expression; disability-related considerations; cultural responsiveness; and the effects of power imbalances, racial trauma and lived experience on participation and evidence.
Applies an equity and human rights lens when assessing allegations, planning interviews, communicating with participants, identifying relevant evidence and preparing findings, while preserving the investigator’s duty to remain neutral, impartial,
Handles sensitive workplace issues and personal information in a responsible, professional and confidential manner, disclosing information only where necessary for the investigation, corrective action, legal compliance, safety, or another legitimate business purpose.

Joignez-vous à l’équipe de Développement des affaires en assurance, au poste de représentant de comptes bilingue, Relations clients – Immeubles collectifs.
Dans ce rôle, vous agirez comme principal point de contact pour les prêteurs afin de leur offrir des conseils et un soutien concernant les produits, politiques, processus et outils d’assurance prêt hypothécaire pour immeubles collectifs, ainsi que les politiques, processus et outils de la SCHL. Ce rôle exige une approche résolument centrée sur le client, une excellente maîtrise de la gestion des relations d’affaires et de la communication dans les deux langues officielles, ainsi que la capacité d’obtenir d’excellents résultats dans un environnement dynamique et en constante évolution.

répondre aux demandes des prêteurs relatives aux produits, politiques, processus et outils d’assurance prêt hypothécaire pour immeubles collectifs, en assurant un service professionnel, exact et opportun, tout en favorisant l’établissement de relations durables avec la clientèle;

analyser les tendances relatives aux demandes de renseignements, la qualité des dossiers soumis et les commentaires des clients afin de cerner les problèmes récurrents et de recommander des améliorations aux processus ou des initiatives de formation;

collaborer avec l’équipe Développement des affaires (DA) – Immeubles collectifs, pour assurer l’harmonisation, le partage des connaissances et le soutien coordonné axé sur les relations avec les clients;
contribuer aux initiatives d’amélioration continue visant à accroître l’efficacité opérationnelle, à optimiser l’expérience client et à promouvoir l’excellence du service.

un diplôme de premier cycle dans un domaine pertinent comme l’administration des affaires, les finances, l’économie ou le commerce, ou une combinaison équivalente d’études et d’expérience;
au moins cinq années d’expérience dans le secteur des services financiers, de préférence dans des postes de première ligne ou de développement des affaires;
de bonne connaissance des pratiques de prêt hypothécaire ainsi que des produits d’assurance prêt hypothécaire de la SCHL, notamment ceux applicables aux immeubles collectifs résidentiels;
un fort sens du service à la clientèle et de la gestion des relations d’affaires, avec une aptitude démontrée à gérer les demandes de renseignements de façon efficace, professionnelle et judicieuse;
d'excellentes aptitudes pour la communication orale et écrite dans les deux langues officielles (anglais et français);

un expérience démontrée en résolution de problèmes, sens de l’initiative et capacité à analyser l’information afin de générer des renseignements exploitables;
une capacité démontrée à collaborer efficacement avec des intervenants internes et externes.

de l'expérience en assurance prêt hypothécaire (APH) pour immeubles collectifs, notamment en ce qui concerne les produits, les outils et les exigences relatives aux demandes;
l'expérience du soutien ou de la prestation d’initiatives de formation, y compris des présentations et du matériel d’information à l’intention de la clientèle;

Join the Insurance Business Development team, in the Bilingual Account Representative, Client Relations – Multi-Unit position.
In this role, you will act as a key point of contact for lenders, providing guidance and support on CMHC’s multi-unit (MU) mortgage loan insurance products, policies, processes, and tools, while building and maintaining strong client relationships.
You will help strengthen client relationships by analyzing trends, identifying opportunities for targeted training, and recommending process improvements. You will also deliver training sessions and support lender-facing initiatives related to CMHC’s multi-unit mortgage loan insurance products.
This role requires a strong client service mindset, excellent relationship management and communication skills in both official languages, and the ability to thrive in a fast-paced, agile environment.
This is a temporary position with a duration of 24 months.

Respond to lender inquiries related to multi-unit mortgage loan insurance products, policies, processes, and tools, ensuring a timely, accurate, and professional service while strengthening client relationships.
Monitor and manage inquiry volumes across various intake channels, ensuring appropriate follow-ups and resolution within established service standards.
Guide lenders through MU MLI application requirements and support the submission of complete, high-quality applications.
Foster strong client relationships by delivering consistent, positive, and relationship-focused client experience in every interaction.
Analyze inquiry trends, submission quality, and client feedback to identify recurring issues and recommend process improvements or training initiatives.
Support the development and delivery of training initiatives, including delivering engaging presentations, webinars, and client-facing materials.
Collaborate with the MU Bdev team to ensure alignment, knowledge sharing, and coordinated relationship-driven client support.
Contribute to continuous improvement initiatives focused on operational efficiency, client experience, and service excellence.
What you should have:
An undergraduate degree in a relevant field such as business administration, finance, economics, or commerce, or an equivalent combination of education and experience.
A minimum of five years of experience in the financial services industry, preferably in client-facing or business development roles.
Knowledge of mortgage lending and CMHC mortgage loan insurance products, particularly for multi-unit residential properties.
Strong client service and relationship management orientation, with the ability to manage inquiries effectively, professionally, and with sound judgment.
Excellent oral and written communication skills in both official languages (English and French).
Strong organizational skills with the ability to manage multiple priorities and deadlines in a fast-paced, agile environment.
Demonstrated problem-solving skills, resourcefulness, and ability to analyze information to generate actionable insights.
A proven ability to collaborate effectively with internal and external stakeholders.
It would be great if you also had:
Experience with multi-unit mortgage loan insurance (MLI), including products, tools, and application requirements.
Experience supporting or delivering training initiatives, including presentations and client-facing materials.
Knowledge of multi-unit underwriting.

Il assure le suivi du rendement des placements en ce qui concerne les actifs et les fonds et fournit des rapports et des analyses connexes. Le titulaire a une bonne connaissance du secteur des placements, notamment en ce qui a trait à la gestion de portefeuille, aux courtiers en valeurs mobilières et en placements et aux régimes de retraite publics, et il connaît bien les marchés financiers. Description de l'emploi
L’agent, Renseignements sur la fraude est responsable de la prestation de solutions analytiques de pointe pour fournir des observations stratégiques à l’équipe de sécurité. Il travaillera avec les membres de l’équipe pour consigner les exigences et élaborer des solutions et des produits de données novateurs, en tirant parti de leurs connaissances et observations en analyse de crimes financiers, en modèles statistiques et en environnement de menace au Canada et à l’échelle mondiale, pour assurer la sécurité et la protection continues des actifs, de la réputation, de l’état financier et opérationnel de Postes Canada.
Le poste est principalement axé sur la détermination, l’évaluation et l’atténuation des risques de fraude qui touchent les intérêts de Postes Canada en matière de sécurité en se basant sur des analyses fondées sur le renseignement et des stratégies proactives de prévention de la fraude.
Responsabilités professionnelles
Voici les principales exigences et responsabilités liées au poste d’agent, Renseignements sur la fraude :
Gérer toutes les étapes du cycle de vie de la gestion de l’information, y compris la réception, la diffusion, l’organisation, la protection et l’évaluation des données opérationnelles, d’enquêtes et de détection de la fraude provenant de diverses sources internes et externes, ainsi que l’élaboration de documents d’exigences, de documents de cartographie des données détaillés et des processus de vérification. Consulter et distribuer des renseignements aux intervenants appropriés afin de soutenir l’atteinte des objectifs de sécurité de Postes Canada et de s’assurer que les données sont conservées et supprimées conformément aux lignes directrices sur la gestion des documents.
Établir des liens avec des partenaires d’affaires internes, des organismes d’application de la loi, des institutions financières et des organisations externes afin d’acquérir, d’élaborer et d’intégrer les renseignements sur la fraude, les tendances émergentes et les menaces qui touchent Postes Canada.
Résumer les renseignements actuels et historiques provenant de plusieurs sources de données pour soutenir les observations stratégiques et les processus de prise de décisions grâce à l’automatisation et à la technologie.
Soutenir les solutions et les produits innovants axés sur les données pour améliorer la proposition de valeur en matière de sécurité en veillant à ce que les produits et les solutions en place, comme les feuilles de calcul et les ensembles de données, soient tenus à jour et rapidement accessibles aux agents régionaux et aux opérateurs pour assurer un accès continu aux renseignements essentiels qui permettent de résoudre les incidents.
Se tenir au fait des pratiques et développements en matière de fraude, de crime financier et de renseignements sur les menaces, au Canada et à l’étranger, et communiquer efficacement aux intervenants les tendances pertinentes afin de soutenir les intérêts de l’organisation et de ses clients en matière de sécurité, ainsi que les activités proactives de prévention de la fraude. Assurer le transfert des connaissances aux membres de l’équipe et consigner les procédures administratives pour assurer la continuité des activités.
Responsabilités professionnelles (suite)
Élaborer et présenter des documents d’analyse à l’intention des cadres supérieurs qui résument les méthodologies, la cartographie des flux d’information mettant en évidence les principales sources de données, l’examen des variables prévues et les résultats attendus aux fins d’analyse, entraînant un haut niveau de compréhension des menaces à la sécurité de Postes Canada.
Effectuer l’analyse des données en exécutant des tâches d’exploration de données afin de créer, d’évaluer et d’améliorer les algorithmes (c.-à-d. classification, régression, regroupement et analyse de texte) pour déterminer les structures de données ou créer des modèles uniformes et reproductibles. Tirer parti des techniques d’analyse pour repérer les tendances en matière de fraude, détecter les anomalies et appuyer les enquêtes sur la fraude et les initiatives de prévention axées sur le renseignement.
Contribuer à l’état de préparation et à la résilience de l’entreprise par l’exploration continue et itérative des rendements opérationnels antérieurs qui améliorent la planification des activités et la prise des décisions.
Établir et promouvoir des outils de collaboration pour faciliter l’échange d’idées et de renseignements entre les employés internes et les partenaires externes. Surveiller les progrès et travailler en collaboration avec les autres intervenants des secteurs concernés pour assurer la synergie et l’harmonisation à l’échelle de la fonction ou de l’entreprise.
Élaborer des stratégies simplifiées avec d’autres responsables fonctionnels pour favoriser l’amélioration et le développement continus.
Critères d’admissibilité
Formation
Diplôme universitaire en gestion de la sécurité, en intelligence d’affaires, en ingénierie, en finances, en commerce, en administration des affaires ou dans une discipline quantitative connexe (p. ex., mathématiques ou statistiques)
Titres professionnels, comme Certified Fraud Examiner (CFE) (examinateur de fraude certifié), Certified Financial Crimes Specialist (CFCS) (spécialiste certifié en lutte contre le crime financier) ou un titre semblable, un atout
Expérience
Au moins cinq ans dans le domaine de l’intelligence d’affaires, de la gestion de la sécurité, de la prévention de la fraude, du crime financier, de la gestion du risque, des renseignements de sécurité ou dans un domaine connexe.
Expérience confirmée de travail axé sur des méthodologies telles que la modélisation prévisionnelle, l’établissement des profils, les prévisions de la segmentation, la recherche opérationnelle et l’exploration des données.
Expérience ou connaissance des outils d’analyse avancés, comme SQL, Oracle/Teradata, C, Python, SAP, SAS, et des outils de production de rapports, comme BO/Webi et Tableau. Toute autre expérience liée aux outils de visualisation peut être un atout supplémentaire.

The position is primarily focused on identifying, assessing and mitigating fraud risks affecting the security interests of Canada Post through intelligence led analysis and proactive fraud prevention strategies.
Job Responsibilities
Below are the main job requirements and responsibilities for Officer, Fraud Intelligence:
Manages all stages of the information management lifecycle including the receipt, dissemination, organization, protection and evaluation of operational, investigative and fraud data from various internal/external sources as well as the development of requirement documents, detailed mapping documents and audit processes. Consults and distributes to appropriate stakeholders in order to support the attainment of Canada Post’s security objectives and ensures data is retained/purged as per record management guidelines.
Develops relationships with internal business partners, law enforcement agencies, financial institutions and external organizations to acquire, develop and integrate fraud intelligence, emerging trends and threat information impacting Canada Post.
Synthesizes current and historical information from multiple data sources to support actionable insights and decision-making processes through automation and technology.
Supports innovative data driven products and solutions to increase the function’s security value proposition by ensuring current products/solutions such as spreadsheets and datasets are kept up-to-date and are quickly accessible to field officers and operators ensuring continuous access to critical information resulting in successful incident resolution.
Keeps current with Canadian and international fraud, financial crime and threat intelligence environments and communicates the relevancy of trends effectively with stakeholders to support corporate and customer security interests as well as support proactive fraud prevention activities. Ensures knowledge transfer to team members and documents business processes to ensure future business continuity.
Job Responsibilities (continued)
Develops and presents analytical briefs to senior management that summarizes methodologies, information flow mapping highlighting key data sources, anticipated variables reviewed and expected output for analysis resulting in high level understanding of potential threats to Canada Post’s security.
Performs data analysis by conducting data mining tasks in order to build, evaluate and improve algorithms (i.e. classification, regression, clustering and text analysis) to identify patterns of data and/or to create models that are consistent and repeatable.  Leverages analytical techniques to identify fraud patterns, detect anomalies and support intelligence led fraud investigations and prevention initiatives.
Contributes to the company’s readiness and resilience through continuous and iterative exploration of past business performances which drive business planning and decision-making.
Establishes and promotes collaborative tools to facilitate sharing of ideas and information among internal employees and external partners. Monitors progress and works collaboratively with other stakeholders of outcome areas ensuring synergy and harmonization across the function/company
Develops streamlined-strategies with other functional leads to enable continuous improvement and development.

Education
University degree in Security Management, business intelligence; Engineering, Finance, Commerce, Business Administration or related quantitative discipline (example: Math/Statistics)
Professional designations such as Certified Fraud Examiner (CFE), Certified Financial Crimes Specialist (CFCS) or similar would be an asset.
Experience
Minimum 5 years work experience in business intelligence, security management, fraud prevention, financial crime, risk management, security intelligence or related field;
Demonstrated experience in working with methodologies such as predictive modeling, profiling, segmentation forecasting, operations research and data mining.
Experience and/or knowledge with advanced analytical tools i.e.  SQL, Oracle/Teradata, C, Python, SAP, SAS, and reporting tools: BO/Webi, and Tableau.  Any other visualization tool experience can be an added asset.

Excellent written and oral skills; analytical ability; strong judgment and leadership skills, and the ability to work effectively with peers, stakeholders and senior leaders;

The energy sector is rapidly evolving, offering exciting new opportunities for those who want to make a difference.

Act as a project leader on projects related to market development initiatives. This may include the management of external consultants retained for the same.
Prepare and review contingency plans for problems and situations that might occur, establish a course of action to accomplish long term goals.

Analyze and review market development plans with the OEB and government agencies.
Review and analyze input from Compliance Section and Market Assessment Units and incorporate findings into market development plans.

Participate in the development of Market Rule amendments as required.
Participate in the development and delivery of internal and external training as required.

Requires analytical and organization skills, excellent written and oral communication skills, in order to undertake studies, programs and projects of major issue, to develop strategies, communicate and effectively interface with all contacts involved in accomplishing the work objectives.

Requires a background that allows for broad thinking and high analytical and reasoning skills.

Requires demonstrated leadership experiences to influence and motivate others to work as team members. Requires project management skills to effectively complete work objectives/projects on time and within budget.

Business Unit: Markets and Reliability
Grade/Band: [[payGrade]]

Annual Pay Range: For standard 40-hour work week

Why join us?
The IESO is committed to ensuring Ontario’s electricity system meets the province’s needs today and into the future.
We are charged with purpose
, delivering reliable, affordable, and sustainable electricity for homes, businesses, and communities across the province.
We are energized to grow
, embracing opportunities to shape the future of a dynamic and evolving energy sector while advancing our careers.
We are powered by teamwork
, supported by diverse and passionate colleagues who foster respect, celebrate successes, and thrive on shared achievements. At the IESO, it’s not just what we do—
it’s who we are!
Who we are
Our central role includes managing the provincial power grid in real-time, overseeing and evolving Ontario’s electricity market, engaging with government, municipalities and Indigenous communities, and planning for Ontario’s future electricity needs. Our employees play a key role in driving grid innovation, protecting the system from threats, advancing the province’s energy conservation programs, and forecasting and procuring the electricity resources we’ll need in the decades to come.
This is a unionized position that falls within the
Market Operations Division in the Markets and Reliability Business Unit.
What makes this role exciting
The energy sector is rapidly evolving, offering exciting new opportunities for those who want to make a difference.
As a member of the Control Room Operations Team, the System Operator helps fulfill the IESO’s roles as Reliability Coordinator, Transmission Operator and Balancing Authority for the province of Ontario by administering the IESO Controlled Grid (“ICG”) and the IESO Administered Markets (“IAM”) on a minute-to-minute basis ensuring a reliable, competitively-priced and sustainable electricity supply for the province:
through intense and timely analysis, investigation and execution of control actions;
in compliance with NERC reliability standards and NPCC criteria;
within the Market Rules and relevant Regulations;
through collaborative work with other Operations Team members;
and under the general direction of the Shift Superintendent.
This is a promotion-in-place (PIP) affected role, candidates with lesser qualifications would be considered for a Assistant System Operator role.
What you’ll do
In this role, you’ll make a meaningful impact by contributing to the IESO team and supporting the electricity needs of the province through:
IESO Administered Markets (“IAM”/”Markets”)
Immediately direct generation or shed load to mitigate critical conditions and preserve the integrity and reliability of the Bulk Electrical System (BES).
Coordinate the IAM as per market rules, NPCC criteria and NERC standards.
Manage the inputs to the Dispatch Scheduling and Optimization engine (“DSO”), review the solution (both real-time (multi-interval optimization (“MIO”)) and pre-dispatch) to ensure accuracy, prepare to manually intervene in the solution if required, and provide final approval of the IAM 5-minute dispatch to maintain the balance of load and generation.
Monitor/identify/investigate/resolve problems in the real-time and pre-dispatch schedules.
Monitor/assess/recommend/implement/reconcile ancillary services contracts (e.g. voltage support, regulation) to meet market rule requirements and recommend further actions if the contract requirements are not being met.
Implement interchange transactions between the IESO and its interconnected neighbours.  This includes verifying the accuracy of NERC E-Tags, curtailing tags as required and providing final approval or denial of E-tags and transactions.
Liaise with neighboring Reliability Coordinators (“RC”) and Balancing Authorities (“BA”) to ensure all interchange schedules are correct and agreed to.  This includes working to resolve disagreements in schedules and arriving at an agreed to solution.
Monitor/assess/implement the required control actions to maintain inadvertent interchange as low as possible as per procedures.
Provide final approval for all planned generation outages, and implement connection and disconnection of generators from the ICG into the market tools.
Implement demand response programs (e.g. OPA DR3 program) as per procedures and direct participants accordingly.
Implement time error corrections and control actions as directed.
Reconcile daily reports such as inadvertent, market reports, etc.
IESO Controlled Grid (“ICG”/”System”)
Immediately direct generation, reconfigure transmission or shed load to mitigate critical conditions and preserve the integrity and reliability of the BES.
Coordinate the operation of the ICG as per market rules, NPCC criteria, NERC standards and Operating Agreements.
Monitor/assess/validate/update Operating Security Limits (“OSLs”) used to maintain system reliability throughout the day.
Monitor/assess/implement/direct the operation of the ICG to maintain all equipment within the ratings provided by market participants, including day-to-day voltage control and power quality.
Monitor/assess/implement/direct items to provide Area supply, provide ancillary services, maintain pre- and post- contingency voltage, respect thermal and stability limits, implement control actions, and respect transmission capacity and tie-line capacity between the IESO and its interconnected neighbors.
Implement industry-based processes and procedures as required (e.g. Intertie Distribution Calculator (“IDC”), Transmission Loading Relief (“TLR”), etc.).
Recognize deficiencies/errors in displays and drawings and recommend and request revision.
Run system studies to determine the effect of different generation and transmission configurations upon the ICG.  Provide recommendations to the Senior Operations Officer.
System for Markets (“SFM”)
Create/check for accuracy/publish System Status Reports (“SSR”) for current day and next day to notify the market place of the status of the ICG and IAM.
Manage the inputs required for the Energy Management System (“EMS”) and DSO to ensure an accurate, consistent and economical solution.
Monitor/assess/recommend/implement hourly changes to items such as Operating Reserve, Area Supply, OSLs, loop flows, post-contingency conditions, transmission capacity and inter-tie capacity to ensure an accurate, consistent and economical solution.
Ensure the accuracy of the OSL activation plan.  Manage and create OSL limits as directed for unplanned outages and out-of-scope conditions.
Monitor/assess/approve/deny the submission of offers and bids into the IAM as per Market Rules.
Submit offers on behalf of market participants in the event of market participant tool failures.
Run reports and produce the daily energy summary report for the Shift Superintendent used in the Morning Report.
Select re-preparation actions as directed and required.
Contingency Operation and System Restoration
Have knowledge and implement contingency plans in preparation for the loss of a generator or transmission system element to maintain the reliability of supply throughout the ICG and protect the integrity of the Eastern Interconnection.  This includes actions that are not documented and require staff to develop and implement plans based on good operating practice, operating agreements and equipment ratings with the cooperation of affected market participants.
Implement demand limits as directed for out-of-scope conditions.
Recommend plans and direct market participants to remove equipment from service.
Plan/coordinate/supervise/direct the actions of internal (Ontario) and external (outside Ontario) entities for system restoration following a major system disturbance or energy emergency. This may include operation that is beyond the scope of past practice and may require execution of undocumented actions.
Implement actions as directed to manage the IAM and ICG following a full or partial loss of the EMS and/or MIS systems.
Outage Plan
Assess/coordinate/revise the outage plan accordingly as real-time approaches to accommodate any changes required.
Assess any short notice and forced outages that may affect the outage plan for the day and change the outage plan accordingly.
Work with market participants to review switching plans to determine if they meet system requirements.
Work with market participants to ensure the accuracy of outage data.  This includes start/end times, correct equipment isolated and that all information is kept up-to-date.
Enter forced/planned outages on behalf of market participants when required and provide an electronic response.
Have an understanding of the impact of generation and transmission outages and the way they are processed in the EMS and DSO systems to ensure a proper outcome.
Notify Operations Planning staff (i.e. those IESO staff that prepare and deliver the daily Operating Plan) of all critical forced outages and extensions that affect their time-frame.
Provide Final Approval for all planned generation and transmission outages.
Tool Set
Have an understanding of the DSO and EMS systems - how they are different and how inputs such as OSL’s and outage slips are handled differently.
Have an understanding of how all the individual programs work on both the EMS and MIS systems and how to manipulate the inputs to achieve the required results.
Perform general performance checks each shift to ensure the results produced are correct.
Identify performance issues to the appropriate support staff for repair.
Perform a detailed assessment of the performance of the EMS and MIS systems following Network Model Builds and software releases.
Coaching, Mentoring and Training
Contribute to the “training” program to ensure that department staffing is adequate as it relates to the certification and technical requirements of the operations functions.  This includes coaching/mentoring junior staff, exercising periodic/limited supervision over designated Control Room staff mainly directed to work assignment, checking work and giving instruction.
Obtain and continually train to complete the required CEH hours to maintain NERC certification as per NERC standards.  Keep up-to-date on advancements or changing technology, government policy, programs, NPCC criteria and NERC standards pertinent to the field of system operations.
Conduct special studies/analyses of market and/or system operations as required.
Off-Shift Assignments

Summarize demand observations, forecasts and deviations into daily reports

Support the integration of short–term demand observations into the medium- and longer-term demand forecasts.

.
Job Overview
Reporting to Senior Manager, Strategic Initiatives, this position is responsible to support the Enterprise Strategy Team in developing insights, analysis and materials that inform enterprise strategy, business planning and strategic decision-making. This role carries out research and analysis, monitors business and industry developments, supports strategic planning activities and helps translate complex information into clear and actionable insights.   The Business Analyst works collaboratively across OPG, building relationships with cross functional teams to gather and share information, validate analysis and support delivery of high-quality presentation materials.
Key Accountabilities
Provide business process support and analytical expertise to the Department Supervisor/Manager, , identifying opportunities to improve how strategic information, analysis and reporting are collected, organized and presented.
Conduct research and monitor trends industry, market, economic, regulatory, policy, and  technology  developments, impacting the  energy sector using a structured and analytical approach, identifying opportunities, risks, and implications for the business.
Gather, organize and analyze information related to market intelligence, business management, performance reporting, benchmarking activities, and new business development opportunities.
Collaborate with internal stakeholders and cross-functional teams across OPG to develop business insights, support informed decision-making, and advance corporate strategic objectives.
Develop business intelligence summaries, briefing notes, presentations, and decision-support materials by synthesizing complex and often unstructured information from multiple sources into clear, actionable insights.
Support the development and refresh of corporate and business strategies, plans and strategic initiatives. Prepare and deliver reports on business performance measures, including analysis of actual results against targets, trends, key metrics, and recommendations for continuous improvement.
Coordinate and facilitate meetings, workshops, and intelligence-sharing sessions; track action items, maintain documentation, and support project management and strategic initiative activities.
Communicate business intelligence findings, analytical insights, and strategic recommendations to stakeholders at various levels of the organization, including senior leadership and executives, while supporting training and knowledge-sharing initiatives.
Qualifications
Completion of a four-year university degree in Business Administration, Economics, Finance, or related discipline. An MBA or relevant industry experience is considered an asset.
Minimum of 2 years and up to 4 years of progressive experience performing business analysis, strategic analysis, market intelligence, or performance reporting within a complex organizational environment.
Demonstrated experience analyzing business processes, operational performance, and organizational data to identify trends, opportunities, efficiencies, and areas for improvement.
Experience researching industry, market, or sector developments and translating findings into business intelligence summaries, briefings, presentations, and actionable recommendations for decision-makers.
Strong analytical, problem-solving, critical thinking, and decision-making skills, with the ability to synthesize complex, unstructured information from multiple sources into clear and concise insights.
Experience developing reports, dashboards, presentations, business cases, briefing materials, and executive-level communication using tools such as Microsoft PowerPoint, Excel, Word, and related business applications.
Knowledge of planning, budgeting, performance reporting, business economics, benchmarking methodologies, decision-support systems, financial modelling concepts, and business information systems.
Excellent interpersonal, communication, and stakeholder management skills, with demonstrated ability to collaborate across teams, facilitate discussions, coordinate activities, and present information effectively to diverse audiences, including senior leadership.
The successful candidate will exhibit uncompromising integrity and commitment to upholding corporate values, and the OPG Code of Business Conduct.
OPG is committed to fostering an inclusive, equitable, and accessible environment. If you require accommodation during the selection process, please contact
AODA@opg.com
.
What makes a career at OPG different?
With operations across Ontario, OPG is one of the most diverse power producers in North America. As the largest generator in Ontario, we meet approximately 50% of the province’s electricity needs, largely from low-carbon sources like nuclear and hydro.
As we work to achieve our vision of Electrifying life in one generation, OPG and our family of companies are also helping advance the development of new low-carbon technologies such as Small Modular Reactors (SMRs), refurbishment projects, and electrification initiatives to help power the growing demands of a growing economy. Join OPG and make history.
The Darlington New Nuclear Project is leading the way in the advancement of
Small Modular Reactor
(SMR) technology in Canada – the future of nuclear power generation! Using new and innovative technologies such as small modular reactors, hydrogen and battery storage, while expanding our hydroelectric and nuclear portfolios, we are changing the electricity landscape in Ontario.

Results-oriented with the ability to learn quickly, work effectively in a fast-paced and changing environment, and manage multiple projects and competing priorities simultaneously.
Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to influence and communicate effectively with internal and external stakeholders at all organizational levels.
Excellent leadership, judgement, decision-making, critical-thinking, and creative problem-solving skills.
High proficiency with information technology tools, including Microsoft Word, Excel, and Power BI, with an ability to use technology to efficiently collect, analyze, and share information.
Hands on experience using large financial or integrated enterprise systems such as SAP, Asset Suite 9, and Anaplan.

title: Director, Customer Technology - Digital Technology Solutions (Toronto, ON, CA)
description:
Position Summary
The Director, Customer Experience – DTS is accountable for the end-to-end technology experience supporting Hydro One’s customers, spanning digital channels, billing, CRM, integrations, service reliability, and enablement platforms. This role leads multiple customer-facing technology portfolios and managers, translating enterprise strategy into predictable delivery, resilient operations, and continuous experience improvement. The role is accountable for predictable, cost-disciplined delivery of customer
‑
critical technology initiatives, ensuring outcomes are delivered on time and within approved budgets.
Core Accountabilities
Customer Experience & Service Outcomes
Own the technology enablement of customer experiences across digital channels, CRM, billing platforms, and supporting integrations.
Ensure service reliability, performance, and responsiveness for customer-facing systems, including accountability for major incidents and root-cause remediation.
Translate customer and business needs into prioritized roadmaps that balance experience improvement, risk reduction, cost, and technical sustainability.
Strategy Execution & Portfolio Delivery
Translate DTS and enterprise strategy into executable plans, funded programs, and committed delivery outcomes.
Accountable for delivering portfolios and major initiatives on time, within approved scope, and on budget, proactively managing risks, dependencies, and trade-offs.
Oversee delivery across multiple application portfolios, including roadmaps, sustainment, enhancements, and modernization initiatives, with clear financial and delivery discipline.
Ensure investments remain aligned to business priorities with transparent cost management, sequencing, and delivery commitments.
Enterprise Platforms & Transformation
Provide domain leadership for major enterprise transformations, including SAP S/4HANA implementations and CRM modernization.
Ensure customer experience, billing, and service processes remain stable and integrated through large-scale system change.
Operational Excellence & Risk Management
Accountable for application sustainment, SLAs, and continuous improvement across customer-critical systems.
Own financial and delivery risk within the domain, ensuring cost controls, forecasting accuracy, and corrective actions are in place.
People & Leadership
Lead, coach, and develop managers with accountability for delivery, budgets, and outcomes.
Build and sustain teams with strong delivery discipline and financial ownership.
Financial & Delivery Accountability
Own the Customer Experience DTS operating and project budgets, including planning, forecasting, and in-year management.
Ensure effective CapEx and OpEx management, vendor spend control, and benefits realization.
Hold teams and partners accountable for predictable delivery and cost transparency.
Required Experience & Qualifications
Technical & Professional Background
Degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or equivalent practical experience.
10+ years of progressively senior technology experience, with early career time spent in the technical weeds (software development, web engineering, systems integration, or application operations).
Strong background in web technologies, including modern web architectures and customer-facing digital platforms.
Extensive experience with CRM platforms supporting customer interaction, workflows, and digital engagement.
Hands-on leadership experience with SAP S/4HANA implementations impacting customer, billing, or revenue processes.
Proven ownership of enterprise platforms across the full lifecycle.
Demonstrated leadership in major incident management and service recovery.
Why This Role Matters
This role ensures Hydro One’s most critical customer and revenue-enabling platforms—web, CRM, digital channels, billing, and S/4HANA-integrated systems—are reliable, scalable, and continuously improving, even through large-scale enterprise transformation.

Job Function:
Hydro One's real estate portfolio is essential to powering the province and supporting thousands of employees across Ontario. The Senior Manager, Real Estate Strategy & Planning serves as a key strategic leader responsible for developing long-term capital plans, overseeing portfolio financials, managing Hydro One's leasing program, and ensuring effective administration of property tax and land rights obligations. Working at the intersection of strategy, finance, and real estate, this role provides the insight, analysis, and planning required to make informed investment decisions and maximize value from the portfolio. The position offers an opportunity to influence enterprise priorities, engage with senior leaders, and help shape the future of Hydro One's workplaces and facilities.
General Accountabilities:
Work collaboratively with Director and CoE Leads to develop F&RE strategy and support investment/business plan, metrics and divisional objectives in each of the key work programs. Work in close collaboration with peer managers to assist in the development of investment/business plans in the various F&RE departments and integrate them into an overall F&RE divisional investment/business plan.
Establish and implement a balanced scorecard and be accountable for any related reporting.
Act as the single point of contact for LoB and enterprise planning and reporting related to F&RE. Establish executive dashboard to track and report all functional metrics. Translate strategic objectives into distinct KPIs.
Benchmark portfolio performance and work to ensure there is a process to continuously improve portfolio management.
Remain current on leading practices in order to improve F&RE performance analytics, risk management, governance, and reporting. Be able to separate 'planning' from 'execution' to enable a focused effort.
Improve asset financial performance through OM&A expense reduction or revenue generation.
Coordinate communication with managers from other parts of Hydro One, ensuring that the F&RE strategy is properly synchronized with the strategic plans in the other lines of business.

Coordinate all investment and business planning activities in the F&RE division. Communicate and coordinate with the senior managers from the F&RE division.

Work with various F&RE managers to determine ways of improving efficiency and productivity across the F&RE functions. Provide guidance on best practice in service level agreement measures, incentive/penalty programs, and progress tracking methods.
Participate in meeting legal, regulatory and market rules requirements by developing information related to outsourcing strategies, policies, and standards, results as required to support submissions to the Regulator. The successful candidate will play a critical role in advancing Hydro One's First Nation Equity Partnership model, helping ensure that our commitments translate into lasting economic opportunities, strong governance, and mutually beneficial outcomes for First Nation partners and future generations.
This is more than a leadership role. It is an opportunity to contribute to a new way of working together, where partnerships are founded on respect, collaboration, and shared success.
About the role
Reporting to the Vice President, Indigenous Partnerships & Business Development, the Director, Indigenous Partnerships – Operations & Governance provides strategic leadership for Hydro One's growing portfolio of First Nation equity partnerships.
As the senior leader responsible for partnership governance, relationship stewardship, and operational performance, you will work closely with First Nation leadership, partner organizations, community representatives, and Hydro One business units to ensure partnerships remain strong, sustainable, and aligned with the priorities of all parties.
You will recognize that every First Nation is unique and will approach each relationship with humility, transparency, respect, and a genuine commitment to understanding community priorities, aspirations, and perspectives.
Success in this role is measured not only by financial and operational outcomes, but by the long-term value created for First Nation communities and Hydro One through trusted, enduring relationships.
The Director also leads a team of partnership professionals and serves as a critical connection point between First Nation partners and Hydro One's business units, helping ensure community perspectives, opportunities, concerns, and priorities are understood and reflected in decision-making.
What you'll be responsible for
Building and strengthening relationships
Serve as a trusted relationship leader for Hydro One's First Nation partnership portfolio.
Build, nurture, and sustain meaningful relationships with First Nation leaders, communities, economic development organizations, and business partners.
Support culturally respectful engagement and ensure Indigenous perspectives are incorporated into partnership governance and business decisions.
Help create an environment where partnerships are founded on transparency, accountability, collaboration, and shared prosperity.
Leading Partnership Governance and Performance
Provide strategic oversight of Hydro One's Indigenous partnership portfolio, including governance, operational performance, and long-term sustainability.
Represent Hydro One on partnership boards, governance committees, and other joint decision-making forums.
Lead the implementation and administration of partnership agreements and governance frameworks.
Ensure commitments made to First Nation partners are fulfilled and partnerships continue to deliver value over time.
Advancing Economic Reconciliation
Identify and support opportunities that strengthen Indigenous participation in Ontario's energy sector.
Work collaboratively with partners to advance economic benefits through investment, employment, procurement, and business development opportunities.
Support innovative approaches to Indigenous partnerships that contribute to Hydro One's leadership in economic reconciliation.
Strategic and Financial Leadership
Provide advice to senior leadership regarding partnership opportunities, risks, governance matters, and investment performance.
Oversee partnership planning, budgeting, financial reporting, forecasting, and performance monitoring.
Review financial models, business cases, investment analyses, and partnership economics to support informed decision-making.
Ensure strong financial stewardship, transparency, and accountability across partnership structures.
Leading and Developing People
Lead, mentor, and develop a high-performing team dedicated to partnership excellence.
Foster an inclusive, collaborative, and culturally safe work environment.
Build organizational capability in Indigenous partnership management, governance, and relationship stewardship.
Establish clear goals, priorities, and expectations while supporting employee growth and development.
What you bring
We're looking for an experienced leader who combines strong business acumen with exceptional relationship-building skills and a deep respect for Indigenous communities and cultures.
You may bring experience from Indigenous governments, economic development corporations, Indigenous-owned businesses, infrastructure organizations, utilities, financial institutions, private industry, or other complex partnership environments.
Qualifications & experience
Post-secondary education in Business, Commerce, Finance, Economics, Law, Engineering, Public Administration, Indigenous Studies, or a related field, or an equivalent combination of education, lived experience, and leadership experience.
Minimum 10 years of experience building and maintaining trusted relationships with Indigenous communities, governments, organizations, or businesses.
Demonstrated experience negotiating, structuring, and managing complex partnerships, joint ventures, equity investments, governance arrangements, or similar collaborative business models.
Strong understanding of Indigenous economic development and partnership principles.
Experience working with boards, governance committees, and executive leadership teams.
Strong financial and commercial acumen, including business planning, financial analysis, budgeting, investment evaluation, and reporting.
Excellent communication, facilitation, and consensus-building skills.
Proven ability to navigate complex stakeholder environments and develop solutions that balance diverse interests.
Experience leading and developing high-performing teams.
Indigenous applicants
Hydro One recognizes the value of Indigenous knowledge, lived experience, and leadership.
We strongly encourage applications from First Nations, Inuit, and Métis candidates. Candidates who self-identify as Indigenous and possess the skills, experience, and leadership qualities outlined in this posting are encouraged to apply.
We are committed to creating a culturally safe, respectful, and inclusive workplace where Indigenous employees can thrive and contribute their perspectives, experiences, and leadership.
Why join Hydro One?
This role provides a rare opportunity to help shape one of the most significant Indigenous partnership portfolios in Canada's energy sector.
You will work alongside Indigenous leaders, communities, and Hydro One colleagues to create lasting value, strengthen relationships, and advance a future where economic reconciliation is achieved through meaningful partnership, shared decision-making, and shared prosperity.
Join us in building partnerships that create benefits for generations to come.

Hydro One is proud to be the largest electricity transmission and distribution provider in Ontario, serving nearly 1.5 million customers. We have a long history in the industry with our roots dating back over 110 years to 1906. Since then, we have worked to grow and evolve to meet the changing needs of our customers and communities across Ontario. Today, we’re focused on providing exceptional customer service and ensuring we are building safe communities where we live, work and play.
It’s an exciting time to join the team at Hydro One!
Job Function:
Purchase a broad range of products and services for a wide variety of clients and applications in the Corporation where the procurement issues are primarily commercial. Procure either consultant, construction and other types of services or mechanical and structural, electrical, computer or general products including engineered products where the design, technical specifications, regulatory requirements, quality assurance standards and inspection checks are already established. Process and administer awards involving the most complex commercial issues.
Job Description:
Within the scope of the procurement policy, develop and maintain procurement procedures and buyer guidelines. Liaise with Finance and legal staff to ensure that procedures meet due diligence and commercial requirements. Work with management staff to provide input to the company's procurement strategies, policies and procedures.
Maintain an awareness of conditions in the market place on assigned goods or services and keep stakeholders informed of significant situations. Initiate and participate in the development of procurement strategies in order to maintain capable and competitive sources of supply. Assist with keeping the potential supplier data base current and in identifying and qualifying additional suppliers. Perform commercial evaluations of potential suppliers and refer technical items to the appropriate specialists for evaluation and qualification.
Review requisitions and tendering documents for completeness and accuracy. Determine if there are regulatory, quality assurance or other special technical requirements and refer to product specialists in the requisitioning units or in the company, as required. Ensure that references to terms, conditions, standards, appendices and other relevant documentation are accurately and consistently referenced throughout the document. Check for the availability of standard or surplus material. Verify the requisitioning authority and resolve discrepancies.
Assess the procurement options such as requests for quotations or proposals, or for private or public tenders and determine the most appropriate, taking into consideration the requirements of the requisitioner and of the company. Review the most recent procurement history available for pricing and resourcing information and determine if bulk or blanket orders already exist or should be initiated. Identify and coordinate the preparation and the renewal of bulk and blanket orders for parts and services, such as repair and maintenance contracts and licensing agreements. Prepare releases where bulk orders exist. Verify sole and only acceptable sources and obtain approvals to negotiate, as required.
Prepare and issue bid lists and obtain approvals where there are changes to regulatory or technical requirements. Assist with or prepare the appropriate tendering documents as necessary. Prepare clarifying addenda and keep the requisitioner informed of all changes. Assess the need for standard or special commercial conditions such as corporate seals, bid securities, labour requirements, financial security or parental guarantees. Ensure that the evaluation criteria for consultants is included and is acceptable.
Negotiate contracts for sole and only acceptable source requirements, in accordance with established policies and procedures. Prepare and issue letters of invitation for private tender/proposal requests. Draft and arrange for newspaper advertisements for public tender/proposal requests. Ensure that capable suppliers are alerted to public requests. Coordinate the activities of the requisitioners and others in providing clarifications to potential bidders arranging pre tender/proposal, post-tender/proposal and site meetings and attend as necessary. Issue addenda and extensions, as required.
Participate in the receipt and opening of tenders/proposals, as required. Issue letters and instructions pertaining to the return of tendering/proposal documents and bid deposits. Ensure that the return of late, incomplete tenders/proposals and the withdrawal or cancellation of tenders is done in accordance with company procedures.
Perform the commercial evaluation of tenders, proposals and quotations including price, performance, domestic content, escalation, foreign exchange, duty, progress payments, labour requirements, financial security, manufacturing capability, etc. and refer other items to the appropriate technical specialists for evaluation. Coordinate technical and other evaluation activities to clarify ambiguities, to resolve exceptions and to correct any errors or omissions. Keep the requisitioner informed during the evaluation and award process as considered necessary.
Determine the required purchasing authorities and prepare purchase approval documents. For requisitioner prepared funding documents, check for accuracy and completeness and add notes, as required. Process for approval.
On receipt of approvals, award business to successful bidders. Advise the unsuccessful bidders in accordance with company procedures. Determine the requirement for basic or formal purchase orders or contracts in accordance with established format and guidelines. Prepare awards to facilitate execution by the supplier and easy administration. Confirm acceptance by the supplier and resolve any discrepancies which may arise. Negotiate and obtain financial and parental guarantees in accordance with company requirements.
Perform ongoing administration of assigned contracts. Coordinate and chair award meetings and identify and ensure the attendance of requisitioners and other special resource people who may be required. Expedite and provide status information to requisitioners and to other stakeholders, as requested. Assist in resolving problems related to invoice discrepancies, material rejections, lost or damaged goods and quantity and other discrepancies. Approve progress payments and review and recommend the payment of adjustment payments. Coordinate the negotiation of contract changes after the award. Prepare and process amendment approval documents and instruction notices. Initiate surveillance assignments, where required, by compiling an assignment package consisting of copies of the purchase orders and other required information for inspection. Coordinate and ensure the review and approval of engineering, manufacturing, regulatory, quality assurance and other technical procedures and documentation by specialist staff in the requisitioning, as required. Initiate, maintain and verify the completeness and accuracy of quality assurance and other files required for the administration of contracts.
Make effective recommendations on the effectiveness and efficiency of products and services purchased by the company.
Handle and process, in accordance with regulatory and company procedures, restricted documents for the procurement of security related equipment and materials.
Perform other duties as required.
Selection Criteria:
Education:
Requires a knowledge of the fundamentals of purchasing, inventory control, transportation and quality management, including contract law, materials forecasting and management, negotiating skills, duties and taxes, insurance, foreign exchange and terms of payment, to carry out the purchasing process.
Requires a good knowledge of mathematics and basic financial practices and procedures to perform commercial evaluations, assign taxes and duties and to administer contracts.
Requires a good knowledge of English and negotiating skills to maintain an effective relationship with requisitioners and suppliers.This knowledge is considered to be normally acquired in either a Grade XII education in a secondary school plus up to one year of further concentrated study, or the equivalent education.
Experience:
Requires procurement experience with the various commercial practices involving quotations, tendering, proposals, public advertising, purchase approvals, placement of business, the administration of contracts, etc.
Requires experience to understand the full scope of the company's purchasing requirements, requisitioning sources and the vendor community to provide input to procurement strategies and policies and to develop procurement procedures and buyer guidelines.
Requires experience with financial and legal counsel to ensure procedures meet due diligence and commercial requirements.
Requires experience with private and public tendering processes.
Requires experience purchasing the range of equipment materials and services.
Requires experience to be familiar with the jargon or working language to facilitate communication, to recognize when regulatory and other special requirements apply and have an expertise and proficiency in dealing with procurement assignments, covering a wide variety of clients and applications.
Requires experience to assess the need for special commercial conditions, including Corporate seals, bid securities, labour requirements, financial security and parental guarantees.
Requires experience with construction contracts to understand related estimating practices, terminology and procedures and to understand drawings and sketches.
Requires experience to be able to input, retrieve, update, assemble and modify information using computerized business systems. A period of over eight years, up to and including ten years, is considered necessary to gain this experience.

The Toronto Transit Commission (TTC), North America's third largest transit system and recognized as one of the top places to work in the GTA has introduced its new 2024-2028 TTC Corporate Plan -  Moving Toronto, Connecting Communities which continues the TTC’s legacy of delivering service to hundreds of millions of customers a year. The TTC’s new vision and mission statements also help promote the many environmental, social equity and economic benefits that the TTC provides:
Vision:
Moving Toronto towards a more equitable, sustainable, and prosperous future.
Mission:
To serve the needs of transit riders by providing a safe, reliable, efficient, and accessible mass public transit service through a seamless integrated network to create access to opportunity for everyone.
The full Plan can
be viewed on ttc.ca.
Career Opportunity
We have an opportunity in our Property, Planning & Development Department for a Property & Agreements Coordinator who has extensive related experience in property acquisitions and/or a project infrastructure environment.
What You Will Do
You will be working with the Property section of the Property, Planning and Development Department to identify all necessary temporary/permanent property requirements and easements, initiate and support the negotiation/expropriation process for the aforementioned property interests in accordance with the approved project schedule and budget, and negotiate/coordinate various complex property agreements.
The incumbent will review design submissions associated with the TTC Major Projects and Capital Works Program projects, and liaise with project teams to identify temporary/permanent property requirements to facilitate construction as well as ensure the project requirements are minimized and justified. In addition, Coordinate and support City of Toronto and York Region Real Estate and Legal Departments to facilitate the acquisition of properties and easements, including providing information to support, and testifying as required, at Expropriation Hearings of Necessity.  Review City/Regional Council reports prepared by City/Region Real Estate and/or Legal for all the property requisitions for capital projects.
Your will be responsible to Initiate and support the negotiation/expropriation process for the property interests in accordance with the approved project schedule and budget. Coordinate/lead as appropriate, negotiations affecting property owners including obtaining Permissions to Enter as required.  As well as, Negotiate/coordinate various agreements, which involves liaising with various parties (City of Toronto and York Region Real Estate and TTC Legal, TTC Engineering and Construction Departments, consultants, provincial and federal agencies, and affected property owners) for their timely execution.
As the Property & Agreements Coordinator, you will obtain all project level sign offs on requisition forms for property acquisition/disposal approval, as well as prepare all necessary TTC Board reports to proceed with the process.
In additon to the above you will promote a respectful work and service environment that supports diversity, inclusion, and is free from harassment and discrimination. Provides leadership in the development and implementation of inclusive and accessible policies, programs and/or services for employees and customers in accordance with TTC’s commitments and obligations under the Ontario Human Rights Code (OHRC) and Related Orders, the Accessibility for Ontarians with Disabilities Act (AODA), and TTC’s policies.
What Skills Do You Bring?
Apply analytical skills
Demonstrate appropriate and effective interpersonal communications through various media

Join the TTC and help protect critical transit infrastructure, influence city-building initiatives, and ensure development projects adjacent to TTC properties support safe, sustainable, and successful transit operations in the role of a Development Coordinator.
What You Will Do
In this role, you will coordinate and manage the review of development applications and property transactions that impact TTC lands, infrastructure, and property rights. Acting as a key liaison between developers, consultants, legal representatives, municipal partners, and TTC departments, you will help ensure that developments adjacent to TTC facilities are designed and constructed in a manner that protects TTC operations, assets, and future growth plans.

Career Opportunity
Ready to help shape the future of transit-focused city-building across the Greater Toronto Area? Join the TTC as a Senior Urban Planner and play a leading role in advancing urban planning initiatives, major transit infrastructure projects, strategic real estate priorities, and long-range planning programs that support one of North America's largest transit systems.
What You Will Do
In this role, you will provide specialized professional leadership and expertise in urban planning, real estate development, and strategic planning to support the TTC's capital infrastructure expansion, state-of-good-repair, and operational priorities. You will act as a key planning advisor, working across the organization and with external partners to ensure municipal and provincial planning initiatives align with and support TTC infrastructure, operational, and strategic objectives.
You will serve as the TTC's primary liaison on complex urban planning matters with municipalities, provincial agencies, and key stakeholders, including the Cities of Toronto, Vaughan, Markham, and Richmond Hill, as well as Metrolinx, CreateTO, and provincial ministries. You will manage TTC involvement in long-range planning initiatives such as Official Plans, Secondary Plans, District Plans, feasibility studies, ensuring TTC interests are represented through technical reviews, policy input, stakeholder working groups, and planning recommendations.
The successful incumbent will manage and coordinate the TTC Real Estate Investment Plan (REIP), supporting the development and implementation of strategies that advance city-building initiatives, transit supportive development opportunities, and TTC real estate priorities. You will also work closely with municipal partners and internal stakeholders to identify opportunities for coordination, process improvements, and efficiencies that support capital project delivery.
You will lead planning due diligence activities for capital, state-of-good-repair, and operational projects by reviewing planning policies, development proposals, legislation, permitting requirements, and municipal approvals processes. In this capacity, you will assess impacts, identify risks and opportunities, and provide strategic recommendations that support project land use, design, approvals, schedules, budgets, and long-term operational requirements.
You will monitor and evaluate emerging planning legislation, development policies, and regulatory changes, including the Planning Act, Building Faster Transit Act, Ontario Building Code, and related frameworks, and implement required changes to TTC planning and approvals processes. You will provide guidance on urban planning, development, and real estate matters affecting TTC capital projects, infrastructure protection priorities, and operational interests.
In partnership with internal and external stakeholders, you will prepare briefing notes, board reports, committee reports, presentations, dashboards, metrics, key performance indicators (KPIs), and objectives and key results (OKRs) that support informed decision-making and demonstrate progress on strategic planning initiatives. You will also negotiate and support agreements with municipalities, agencies, and other stakeholders to advance planning priorities and city-building opportunities on TTC lands.
As a trusted subject matter expert, you will establish and maintain strong working relationships across the organization and with external partners, provide professional guidance on complex urban planning and development matters, and contribute to continuous improvement initiatives that enhance planning, approvals, and strategic coordination across the TTC.
What Skills Do You Bring?
Use office technology, software and applications
Apply analytical skills
Secure and manage fiscal resources
Manage projects
Plan and organize activities / projects to meet section and organizational goals
Apply the principles and practices of quality assurance
Maintain documentation and historical records
What Qualifications Do You Bring?
University degree in Urban Planning, Environmental Studies, Project Management, or a related discipline, combined with significant experience in urban planning, land development, planning policy, strategic planning, and/or large-scale transit and infrastructure projects.
Membership in the Ontario Professional Planners Institute (OPPI) or the Canadian Institute of Planners (CIP) or in progress.
Project Management Professional (PMP) designation or in progress, is considered an asset.
Exceptional interpersonal and relationship-building skills, with the ability to effectively engage, influence, and collaborate with a diverse range of internal and external stakeholders.
Demonstrated empathy, emotional intelligence, and the ability to build trust and credibility while navigating complex planning, development, and stakeholder interests.
Open-minded, adaptable, and flexible in approach, with the ability to balance competing priorities and perspectives in a dynamic and evolving environment.
A genuine enthusiasm for urban planning, city-building, transit-supportive development, and shaping communities through long-range planning initiatives.
Strong facilitation and collaboration skills, with the ability to bring people together, build consensus, and serve as a central point of coordination across multidisciplinary teams.
Extensive experience working with municipal and provincial planning processes, approvals, legislation, regulations, policies, and development frameworks.
Comprehensive knowledge of urban planning principles, land development processes, planning policy, real estate development, and development approval systems.
Strong understanding of agreements, leases, contracts, easements, and real estate transaction processes, including negotiation and stakeholder management.
Demonstrated experience managing complex projects and coordinating multiple stakeholders within a fast-paced and politically sensitive environment.
Experience reviewing and interpreting planning studies, planning policies, legislation, development applications, engineering reports, environmental assessments, and technical documentation.

Strong report writing, presentation, communication, facilitation, negotiation, and stakeholder relationship management skills.

A valid, non-probationary Ontario Class G driver's licence in good standing. A licence in good standing is defined as a driver's abstract free of convictions, demerit points, suspensions, collisions, and reportable accidents. Access to a vehicle is considered an asset.
Knowledge of accessibility requirements, disability accommodation principles, and the Ontario Human Rights Code.
